title: Add the arcade-cabinet example
body:
## What this changes

Adds `examples/arcade-cabinet/`, an eighth example: an upright arcade cabinet in the style of 1981, seen from the player's front-left with the left side panel off. About 240 recorded solids and 15 cables.

- **Coin path.** A quarter (24.26 mm) flies from a tray on the bench into the left slot and spends 0.42 s in the mech. It then rolls down a 30° chute at the acceleration a rolling disc gets (2/3 g sin 30°), presses the coin-switch wire and falls into the open cash box, where coins pile up. The six-digit meter counts it.
- **Signal and boot.** The switch's pulse runs chunk by chunk along its cable to the board's edge connector (in depth order, by lighting the tube chunks). The marquee strikes, the CRT heater warms for about 2 s, the board shows a RAM/ROM self-test, and the attract mode starts.
- **The picture.** A 224 × 288 vertical game with an original pixel font and sprites, drawn in the plane of the tilted CRT and clipped by the bezel opening. The recess walls are drawn. The monitor lies on its side, so switching off (Esc) folds the picture to a vertical line, then a dot.
- **Controls.** The stick tilts (← →) and its actuator closes one of four microswitches under the panel, and the ship follows. Space presses the fire button. An idle tour plays the whole sequence.
- **Inside.** CRT with band, ears, funnel, yoke, convergence rings, neck board and anode lead. Monitor frame and shelf, and a chassis board with flyback, heat sink and pots. Game board on the back panel with chips, traces and an edge connector; a braided loom; a rear fan; a power chassis and a service bracket (test, service, volume); an isolation transformer and a switcher.

It also shows a few techniques the other examples don't:
- a prism of a concave section along any axis, used for the side panel and boards;
- moving parts (stick, coin) rebuilt in the page by the same `parts.mjs` the build imports, with `lathe.mjs` inlined in a closure;
- live content placed in reserved slots of the settled order: the coin on the chute and in the box, and the switch wire.

No kit changes, so every other example is untouched. It is added to `SKILL.md`, the README tables, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, CI and `CHANGELOG.md`.

One liberty, stated in the caption: on a real cabinet a coin only adds a credit. Here the coin switch also latches the power relay, so the first coin wakes the machine.

## Why

None of the examples follows a part through a mechanism, and none shows a picture on a tilted plane rather than a vertical face. The cabinet also works through a real cutaway camera problem. From the front, nothing behind a centred coin door can be seen at any angle that still shows the screen. So the door sits toward the open side and accepted coins roll back to a cash box that stays in view.

## Checks

- [x] Every example rebuilds, and `git status --short` shows only the changes I meant. The two new pages rebuild byte-identical on Node 26 on Linux; I haven't run the macOS CI locally.
- [x] No comments in code.
- [x] Kit changes are opt-in: there are none.
- [x] I built and looked at both themes.
- [x] `node examples/arcade-cabinet/build.mjs --audit` ends `audit passed` (15 tubes, 243 solids, 349 items), every failing line at 0.
- [x] `node scripts/lines.mjs` prints `line ends: 0` on both themes and in the switched-off pose.
- [ ] Shaders: none.
- [ ] 3D: none.
- [x] Every number in the figure, the readout, the caption and the docs is true; the one liberty is stated above and in the caption.
- [x] A line under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Screenshots

Light, attract mode:

![light](https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy/blob/pr-assets/arcade-cabinet/light.png?raw=true)

Dark:

![dark](https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy/blob/pr-assets/arcade-cabinet/dark.png?raw=true)

4× close-ups: the picture on the tilted CRT; the coin path (switch, wire, chute, cash box, meter); the CRT neck, yoke and chassis in dark; the stick with its closed switch below the panel edge.

![screen](https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy/blob/pr-assets/arcade-cabinet/screen-light.png?raw=true)
![coin path](https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy/blob/pr-assets/arcade-cabinet/coin-path-light.png?raw=true)

title: fix: fail browser drives on evaluation errors
body:
## What this changes

Make browser evaluations in `scripts/drive.mjs` reject Chrome protocol errors and JavaScript exceptions, including awaited promise rejections. Keep successful JSON and `undefined` evaluations working. Add seven dependency-free browser CLI regressions to CI and document their command.

## Why

A documented `eval` action that throws an assertion currently prints `eval: undefined`, reports `console: clean`, and exits successfully. Synchronous errors, rejected promises and syntax errors all reproduce this false success. An exception in an `until` condition also loses its actual error and eventually reports a timeout instead.

## Checks

- [x] Every example rebuilds, and `git status --short` shows only the changes I meant.
- [x] No comments in code.
- [x] Kit changes are opt-in, and every existing example is byte-identical (or this PR says which pages change and why).

- [ ] Figures with pipes, cables or round parts: `node build.mjs --audit` ends `audit passed`, every failing line at 0.
- [ ] `node scripts/lines.mjs` prints `line ends: 0` on both themes and in every resting pose.
- [ ] Shaders: a slowed contact sheet across every transition shows no pop, and `--no-webgl` still reads.
- [ ] 3D: a full run ends `turn audit passed`, and `scripts/turn-check.mjs` passes.
- [x] Every number in the figure, the readout, the caption and the docs is true.
- [x] A line under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`.

Visual checks are unticked because this changes only verification tooling; every committed example page rebuilds byte-identically in both themes, including the turning verification and stress pages. Kit APIs, geometry, shaders and figures are untouched.

`node --test scripts/drive.test.mjs`: the original driver fails four assertions and passes three controls; the fixed driver passes all seven tests without skips. Tests launch actual headless Chrome with throwaway profiles and owned local fixtures. Three original error cases exit 0; the fourth is an `until` error-context failure, not a successful exit. Successful JSON, `undefined` and wait-condition controls pass.

Local verification uses Node 24.18.0 and Chrome 154. The [full fork CI](https://github.com/rudycelekli/anatomy/actions/runs/38108215085) passed on macOS with Node 22: all seven actual Chrome regressions, every example rebuild and the final clean-tree check. The workflow checked out and asserted the exact application commit `1c63574356e4466e71cdf99cd0e79b9bdfad45f8`.

title: fix(arcade): accept inserted coins with reduced motion
body: ## What this changes Accept an inserted coin when reduced motion skips directly to its landing pose. Keep the existing `c.switched` guard so each coin increments the meter and awards credit exactly once. Rebuild the light and dark arcade pages. ## Why With reduced motion enabled, `c.t` advances by 10 seconds on the first frame. The coin is already in the drop stage, so the rolling-stage switch condition never runs. A coin leaves the tray, but the cabinet stays off, the meter stays at `004127`, and no credit is awarded. After this change the same input powers on the cabinet, increments the meter to `004128`, and shows `credit 1`. Reduced motion skips the animation while preserving its functional result. Reproduce: emulate `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, open either arcade page, focus the figure, and press `c`. ## Checks - [x] Every example rebuilds; all 14 CI build commands passed and only the intended pages differ. - [x] No comments added to code. - [x] No kit API changes; generated-page differences are described above. - [x] A line under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`. - [x] Built and inspected both themes, including 4× close-ups. - [x] Arcade geometry audit ends `audit passed`, with zero reported failures. - [x] Line-end checks report 0 failures in both themes after reduced-motion insertion. - [x] One coin, three coins, ordinary motion, and switching to reduced motion during a coin's flight all pass in both themes. - [x] At 390px width with WebGL disabled, the same interaction checks pass without JavaScript errors or horizontal page overflow. - [x] Observed meter, credit, and power state agree: one coin adds one credit; three coins add three. - [ ] Shader transition contact sheets: not run; shader code and animation envelopes are unchanged. The SVG fallback was checked. - [ ] 3D orbit audit: not applicable; this change is in the arcade's 2D animation state logic. ## Screenshots Before/after comparisons in both themes and 4× close-ups are attached below. title: fix(turning-dial): stop touring when reduced motion is enabled
body: ## What this changes When the frame loop observes reduced motion, stop the automatic tour and cancel the pending idle restart. Rebuild the light, dark, and verification pages; the stress page stays byte-identical. Manual input remains available. After reduced motion is disabled, the dial stays at its current pose until input; subsequent input uses the existing idle-tour restart behavior. ## Why The tour flag is initialized from the preference at page load. Enabling reduced motion during an active tour updates `still.matches` but leaves that flag true, so the dial keeps rotating at approximately 18 degrees per second. Reproduce: load the turning dial with normal motion, let the tour start, then change `prefers-reduced-motion` to `reduce` without reloading. Before this change it keeps turning. After this change it settles and stays still. ## Checks - [x] Every example rebuilds; all 14 CI build commands passed and only the intended pages differ. - [x] No comments added to code. - [x] No kit API changes; generated-page differences are described above. - [x] A line under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`. - [x] Built and inspected both themes, including 4× close-ups. - [x] Enabling reduced motion during a tour leaves the sampled angle unchanged: delta 0° in both themes, versus approximately 20–21° before over the sampling interval. - [x] Keyboard input still changes the angle under reduced motion; waiting beyond the idle timeout does not restart the tour. - [x] Loading with reduced motion already enabled stays still. - [x] Disabling reduced motion, providing input, and waiting for the normal idle timeout restarts the tour. - [x] The same checks pass at 390px width with WebGL disabled, without JavaScript errors or horizontal page overflow. - [x] Fidelity check passes across 12 angles; intentionally bad control is detected. - [x] Line-end checks pass in both themes across the sampled angles. - [x] Painter-order check passes at 1° steps through 360 states; reverse-order control is detected. - [x] Full 3D audit ends `turn audit passed` (589.95 seconds); geometry audit also passes. - [x] Readout angle matches the observed stationary pose after reduction. - [ ] Shader transition contact sheets and exhaustive joint/performance certification: not run; this fix changes tour control flow, not geometry or shaders. Both themes and the SVG fallback were inspected. ## Screenshots Before/after time-pair comparisons in both themes and 4× close-ups are attached below. The after pair stays at the same angle after reduced motion is enabled.

title: fix(drive): fail when an until action times out
body:
## What this changes

Throw when an `until` action reaches its deadline without a truthy result. The existing error handler then closes the drive session and exits with status 1. Update the action help text to describe this behavior.

## Why

A timed-out wait currently prints a message, runs later actions, and exits 0. This can make a failed browser check appear successful or produce screenshots before the intended state exists.

Related: #2 handles evaluations that throw or reject. This fixes a different case: evaluation succeeds but continues returning `false`. I reproduced that timeout behavior on #2's head commit `1c63574356e4466e71cdf99cd0e79b9bdfad45f8` as well as current main. This PR does not duplicate its evaluation-error handling.

Minimal reproduction, using an actions file as the driver documentation recommends:

```sh
cat > /tmp/anatomy-until.json <<'JSON'
[["until","false",100],["eval","'ACTION_AFTER_TIMEOUT'"]]
JSON
node scripts/drive.mjs examples/dial-indicator/dial-indicator-light.html --actions /tmp/anatomy-until.json
echo "exit=$?"
```

Before: timeout message, `ACTION_AFTER_TIMEOUT`, `console: clean`, exit 0.
After: `Error: until: timed out waiting for false`, exit 1; the marker action does not run.

## Checks

- [x] Every example rebuilds; all 14 CI build commands passed and only the intended pages differ.
- [x] No comments added to code.
- [x] No kit API changes; generated-page differences are described above.
- [x] A line under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`.
- [x] Always-false condition exits 1 and stops subsequent actions.
- [x] Immediately true and delayed-success conditions exit 0 and execute subsequent actions.
- [x] Combined with #2's evaluation wrapper: its seven browser tests and all three timeout/success regressions pass.
- [x] All committed example pages rebuild byte-identically.
- [ ] Both themes, geometry, line ends, shaders, 3D audit, figure numbers: not applicable to this CLI control-flow change; figure source and generated pages are unchanged.

## Screenshots

Not applicable. This is a CLI exit-status change; the reproducible command and before/after output above demonstrate the behavior.

Audit distance checks replace every variable-radius tube segment with a cylinder at its averaged radius. This invents collisions near the narrow end and misses them near the wide end, despite recording the actual taper. The existing Raptor builder records the affected per-point tube radii. These are software geometry checks, not physical measurements.

title: fix(lines): respect Bezier continuation control families
body:
## What this changes

The line verifier shares one untyped control point between cubic and quadratic curves. A smooth cubic after a quadratic, or smooth quadratic after a cubic, reflects the wrong control and misses lines rooted on the actual SVG stroke. Keep the control’s curve family and reflect it only for a matching continuation; existing same-family curves retain their behavior.

## Checks

title: fix(drive): await asynchronous until conditions
body:
## What this changes

Await the value of an asynchronous `until` expression before checking its truthiness. Enforce the existing deadline even when a returned promise never settles. Add nine browser regressions covering false results, delayed success, rejection, pending promises and synchronous truthy values.

## Why

The driver currently evaluates `Boolean(expression)`. A promise is truthy even when it resolves to false, so `until Promise.resolve(false)` reports success and executes dependent actions. A delayed success also lets later actions run before its promise resolves.

The existing timeout fix in #5 handles synchronous false conditions. This extends the same contract to asynchronous conditions while preserving rejection reporting from #2.

Reproduce with an actions file:

```json
[["until","Promise.resolve(false)",100],["eval","'AFTER_FALSE_PROMISE'"]]
```

Before: prints `AFTER_FALSE_PROMISE`, `console: clean`, and exits 0.
After: reports the failed wait, exits 1, and does not run the next action. A rejected condition reports its original error; a never-settling promise also times out.

## Checks

- [x] New tests reproduce the failure on main before applying the fix.
- [x] No comments added to source or tests.

title: fix(browser-checks): start headless Chrome from an elevated Windows terminal
body:
## What this changes

`capture.mjs`, `drive.mjs` and `turn-check.mjs` pass `--do-not-de-elevate` to Chrome on Windows, next to the `--no-sandbox` they already pass on Linux.

## Why

From an elevated terminal (an administrator PowerShell, which is how some people run their agent on Windows), every browser check fails at once:

```
Error: Chrome exited before startup: 0
```

Chrome relaunches itself without the elevation when its parent is elevated. The process the script spawned exits with code 0 after about 90 ms and prints nothing, so `chromePort` gives up. The relaunched browser keeps running, detached, with its debugging port open and the temporary profile in use, and one is left behind per attempt. Its command line ends in `--do-not-de-elevate`, the switch Chrome adds to its own relaunch. Passing that switch up front keeps the first process as the browser.

Measured on Windows 11 with Chrome 155.0.8059.39 and Node 20.17.0, with one probe that spawns Chrome and waits for `DevTools listening`:

| Parent process | Without the switch | With it |
|---|---|---|
| Elevated (high integrity) | exits 0 after about 90 ms | listening after 136 ms |
| Not elevated (medium integrity) | listening after 161 ms | listening after 132 ms |

Edge and Playwright's Chromium exit the same way without the switch. I tried the switch itself only on Chrome.

title: Recursive subcomponent zoom
body:
### What are you asking for?

Something else

### The idea

A new opt-in prompt option (key value?), `levels=n`, alongside `interactive`, `WebGL` and `3D` . This seems like the missing piece that would make any more complex item more completely explainable... ex. the modular synth: each oscillator unit could be inspected, then from there zoom into the pcb to get a deeper understanding of the component. Or with the watch example, look at an individual gear etc and get an explanation. Or, say, a tube amplifier? I'd love to pull apart the amp then zoom in to the tubes themselves.

`levels=n` lets a figure zoom into a part and show the smaller idea inside it. The skill runs recursively on each subcomponent, so the figure's model becomes a tree n levels deep.

```
/anatomy explain mark-and-sweep garbage collection, interactive, levels=2
```

`levels=1` is today's figure, so nothing changes unless you ask. Each level is an ordinary figure; the only new rules are what passes between parent and child, which could live in `references/depth.md`:

- The child owns a smaller model and the parent reads from it. The synth module's lamp is the mark bit in the header you see when you zoom in, so the levels can't disagree.
- Only parts that hide a real idea of their own open, one or two per level, since each costs about a Figure.
- The zoom stays in the same camera and the same world: lift the module's faceplate and there's a circuit board with a header row and jacks.

Desk computer (computer → CPU → ALU → adder) would be a good first example.

### Why it is worth adding

Many ideas are only understood one level down. Detail at 4× and the exploded view both stay at the same level of the idea, and a second figure doesn't share the first one's model or clock.

`node scripts/publish.mjs … --submit --yes` stops at its first step, "make (or reuse) your fork", for a user without push access to the gallery. `submitPlan` runs `gh repo fork wheresryan22/anatomy-community --clone=false --remote=false`, and gh 2.101.0 refuses the `--remote` flag when a repository argument is given, then prints its help. gh repo fork wheresryan22/anatomy-community --clone=false --remote=false

```shell
the `--remote` flag is unsupported when a repository argument is provided
```

title: fix(ripple-tank): read ink colour from the fixed per-theme uniform
body:
## What this changes

`examples/ripple-tank/live.js`'s paper and water shaders picked their ink colour with `uPale>.5?vec3(.11,.11,.12):vec3(.02,.025,.03)` (and the paper shader's light branch repeated the light half of that same pair), both hardcoded inline in GLSL. Every other per-theme tuned constant in this file — `uExpo`, `uEnv`, `uGlass`, `uGlint`, `uTint`, `uWall` — is instead set once as `pale ? light : dark` in the `FIXED` uniform object passed to `glLayer`. Added `uInk` to `FIXED` next to the others, declared `uniform vec3 uInk;` once in the shared `WAVE_GLSL` prelude, and pointed both shaders at it. Same two colour values, same `pale` switch — only the wiring changed, so the rebuilt pages are pixel-identical to what shipped before.

## Why

CONTRIBUTING.md's house rules state colours are tokens with a light value and a dark override, never literals in a figure's shader. title: scripts: handle spawn errors, sanitize headless DISPLAY, and prevent ReDoS in audit.mjs
body:
### Summary

This PR addresses several resilience and edge-case failure modes across the CLI tools and SVG auditing:

1. **Child Process Error Handling:**
   - In `scripts/turn-check.mjs`, `scripts/drive.mjs`, `scripts/lines.mjs`, and `scripts/capture.mjs`, attached explicit `.on("error")` handlers to spawned child processes (`node --experimental-websocket`, `drive.mjs`, and headless `chrome`). Previously, if binary execution failed (e.g., spawn ENOENT or system process limits), an unhandled `error` event would crash the process with an unhandled rejection.

2. **Headless Linux `DISPLAY` Sanitization:**
   - In headless Chrome invocations across `turn-check.mjs`, `drive.mjs`, and `capture.mjs`, sanitized `DISPLAY` on Linux environments. In containerized or headless setups where an X11 socket isn't authorized for the running user, Chrome's ozone platform would attempt to connect via XCB, throwing authorization failures and breaking WebGL initialization.

3. **Safe Argument File Parsing:**
   - In `scripts/turn-check.mjs` (`--states`) and `scripts/drive.mjs` (`--preload` and `--actions`), wrapped file reading and `JSON.parse` in try/catch blocks that provide clear, informative error messages rather than raw unhandled exceptions if the file is missing or invalid.

4. **ReDoS Prevention in `kit/audit.mjs`:**
   - In `markupBox(svg)`, refactored the tag-matching regex `/<(\/?)([a-zA-Z]+)((?:"[^"]*"|'[^']*'|[^"'\/>]+)*)\s*(\/?)>/g` so the token groups are mutually exclusive, eliminating exponential backtracking on unclosed quotes or malformed SVG input.

5. **Documented Intentional Empty Catches:**
   - Added descriptive comments to empty catch blocks used for best-effort cleanup of temporary browser profile directories, NDJSON session log line parsing, and browser pointer capture release.

### Testing
- Ran all regression and unit tests via `node --test` (95/95 passed cleanly).
- Verified `scripts/orbit-sampling.test.mjs` passes in headless mode without X11 authorization errors.

title: capture.mjs: reject option values it cannot use
body:
## What this changes

`capture.mjs` now checks its option values before it starts Chrome and exits 1 with a one-line message when one cannot be used: `--width`, `--height`, `--scale`, `--zoom-scale` not a number above 0; `--wait` or `--times` negative or non-numeric; `--zoom` not four numbers with a width and height above 0; `--hover` not two numbers; `--theme` not `dark` or `light`.

## Why

Every option goes through `Number(...)` with no check. On current main:

    node scripts/capture.mjs figure.html --wait 0 --out c.png --zoom 1,2   # exit 0, "saved c.png"
    node scripts/capture.mjs figure.html --wait 0 --out c.png --times fast # exit 0, "saved c.png"
    node scripts/capture.mjs figure.html --wait 0 --out c.png --width wide # exit 0, "saved c.png"
    node scripts/capture.mjs figure.html --wait 0 --out c.png --scale 0    # exit 0, "saved c.png"
    node scripts/capture.mjs figure.html --wait 0 --out c.png --theme sepia # exit 0, "saved c.png"

so a mistyped flag produces a picture that looks like a normal capture but ignores what was asked for (I also saw `--zoom 1,2` end in `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'data')` on one run). When the shot is the evidence in a review, a silently ignored `--zoom` or `--theme` is worse than an error.

title: turn-fidelity.mjs: transform upright prisms through their frame before k.extrude
body:
## What this changes

- `scripts/turn-fidelity.mjs`: when `run.up` is true in `identity()`, transform `part.world.ring` and the bottom axial coordinate (`F.a[2] < 0 ? s1 : s0`) through `part.world.F` (`F.o`, `F.u`, `F.v`, and `F.a`) into world XY and world bottom Z before calling `k.extrude`, matching `T.prism` in `kit/turn-build.mjs`.
- `scripts/fidelity-cut.test.mjs`: add regression tests covering upright frame-authored prisms with non-zero frame origins, non-square cross-sections, along-axis vertical splits (`T.split`), and downward vertical frame axes (`F.a = [0, 0, -1]`).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: record the fix under `Unreleased`.

## Why

In `kit/turn-build.mjs`, `T.prism` marks any prism in an upright group with `Math.abs(F.a[2]) > 0.9999` as `upright = true` (`part.spec.up = 1`, `run.up = true`) — including prisms authored via `{ F, polygon, s0, s1 }` as well as every upright prism split by `T.split` (which reconstructs both halves via `T.prism({ ...h, F, polygon })`). `T.prism` stores the untransformed `{ F, ring, s0, s1 }` on `part.world`, and then transforms `ring` at `s = F.a[2] < 0 ? s1 : s0` through `F` (`F.o + s * F.a + x * F.u + y * F.v`) to populate `part.spec.ring`, `part.spec.z0`, `part.spec.z1`, and `part.planPath`.

However, `identity()` in `scripts/turn-fidelity.mjs` passed the raw frame-local `part.world.ring` and `part.world.s0` directly to `k.extrude(ring, s0, s1 - s0, Pk)` whenever `run.up` was true, ignoring `F.o`, `F.u`, `F.v`, and `F.a[2] < 0`:
1. `G.frameAlong(o, [0, 0, 1])` has `F.u = [0, -1, 0], F.v = [1, 0, 0]` (a 90° rotation of XY), so any non-square polygon or any upright prism split along its axis (`T.split(part, { n: [1, 0, 0], d })`) had its cross-section rotated 90° relative to the untransformed `k.extrude` reference.
2. Any upright frame with a non-zero origin `F.o` had its XY translation and Z offset (`F.o[2]`) omitted from the `k.extrude` reference.
3. Any upright frame with a downward vertical axis (`F.a = [0, 0, -1]`) evaluated `k.extrude` at `s0` instead of `F.o[2] - s1` and without reflecting the ring through `(F.u, F.v)`.

The previous test fixture in `scripts/fidelity-cut.test.mjs` only passed because it used `F = G.frameAlong([0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 1])` at the origin with a centered 4×4 square polygon (invariant under 90° rotation) and a horizontal cut plane (`n: [0, 0, 1]`). Transforming `ring` and `s = F.a[2] < 0 ? s1 : s0` through `F` before calling `k.extrude` brings `turn-fidelity.mjs` into exact agreement with `T.prism` while keeping `plan`-authored prisms (`F = { o: [0, 0, 0], a: [0, 0, 1], u: [1, 0, 0], v: [0, 1, 0] }`) identical.

title: Fix 3D tube surface sampling in audit support checks
body:
## What this changes

- Updates the `tube` branch of `surfaceOf(shape, spacing)` in `kit/audit.mjs` to sample points along each sample's 3D perpendicular cross-section via `ringAround(sample, sample.r)` instead of offsetting centerline points by a flat horizontal `XY` circle (`[Math.cos(k * Math.PI / 4), Math.sin(k * Math.PI / 4), 0] * r`).
- Adds regression tests in `scripts/audit-tube-support.test.mjs` covering:
  - Horizontal stiff tubes resting on grounded horizontal tubes (parallel and perpendicular) and supporting mounted solids above them.
  - Horizontal stiff tubes separated from a grounded wall by an air gap beyond their flat end cap being reported as `hanging` (and any solids mounted only to them as `loose`), while still accepting genuine flat end-cap contact within `touch`.
  - Inclined stiff tubes detecting perpendicular contact and rejecting perpendicular air gaps.
  - Vertical stiff tubes and `limp: true` tubes preserving their existing support semantics.
- Records the fix under `Unreleased -> Fixed` in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Why

In `kit/audit.mjs`, `supports(solids, tubes)` calls `surfaceOf(shape)` on every solid and every non-limp (`!tube.limp`) tube to test pairwise contact (`sdf(other, p) <= touch`). Previously, the `tube` branch of `surfaceOf` (line 1088) ignored the local tangent `sample.t` computed by `samplesOf(shape, spacing)` and instead offset each centerline point `p` by `mul3([Math.cos((k * Math.PI) / 4), Math.sin((k * Math.PI) / 4), 0], r)` — a flat horizontal circle in the world `XY` plane (`dz = 0`).

For any non-vertical stiff tube (which also arises in `kit/turn-audit.mjs` when `orbit` poses rotating tubes across 3D orientations), this caused two opposite audit failures:

1. **False-negative support (`hanging` tubes and `loose` solids) across vertical or perpendicular contact**: Because every sampled point had `z = p[2]` (zero vertical offset from the centerline), the top (`z = p[2] + r`) and bottom (`z = p[2] - r`) of a horizontal tube were never sampled. A horizontal stiff tube resting on top of a grounded horizontal tube had minimum sampled distance `r` instead of `0`, so `supports()` falsely flagged it as `hanging` (and any solids supported through it as `loose`) whenever `r > touch` (`0.15`).
2. **False-positive support across an air gap beyond flat end caps**: For a horizontal tube along `X` (`t = [1, 0, 0]`), the horizontal `XY` ring stepped `±r` *along* the tube axis at `k = 0, 4`. At the tube's endpoints (`points[0]` and `points[last]`), this placed sample points up to `r` units outside the flat end cap in empty air (`sdf(tube, p) === +r`), allowing a floating stiff tube separated from a grounded wall by an air gap up to `r + touch` to pass `supports()` as grounded.

Using `ringAround(sample, sample.r)` (already used by `clearances()` in `kit/audit.mjs`) samples 12 points around the true cross-sectional ring perpendicular to `sample.t` at every sample along the tube.

## Checks

title: turn-build: ignore repeated vertices when rounding a prism polygon
body:
## What this changes

`roundedPolygon` in `kit/turn-build.mjs` (used by `T.prism({ polygon, round })`) drops consecutive duplicate points, including a closing point equal to the first, before it rounds the corners.

## Why

Each corner arc is built from the unit normals of the two edges that meet there. A repeated vertex is a zero-length edge, and its normal came out as `[0, 0]`, so the arc at the next corner had the wrong centre and the ring left the polygon. On current main (`bc943e4`):

    roundedPolygon([[0,0],[10,0],[10,10],[0,10]], 1, 2)        // x extent [0, 10]
    roundedPolygon([[0,0],[10,0],[10,0],[10,10],[0,10]], 1, 2) // x extent [0, 11], stray points (10.707,0.293) (11,1), three copies of (10,0)
    T.prism({ polygon: [[0,0],[4,0],[4,0],[4,4],[0,4]], round: 1 }) // max ring x is 5, the polygon ends at 4

The stray ring then feeds the collision shape, the samples and the drawn silhouette of the part.

## Verification

New `scripts/turn-rounded-polygon.test.mjs` (3 tests: a repeated vertex, a repeated first vertex at the end and a triple vertex all give the same ring as the clean polygon; the ring extent stays inside the polygon, both directly and through `T.prism`).

- main: `node --test --test-concurrency=2 scripts/turn-rounded-polygon.test.mjs` gives `# pass 0 / # fail 3`
- with the change: `# pass 3 / # fail 0`
- `node --test --test-concurrency=2 scripts/turn-group-reference.test.mjs scripts/turn-split-owner.test.mjs scripts/fidelity-cut.test.mjs`: 25 pass, 0 fail
- `node examples/turning-dial/build.mjs` and `node examples/arcade-cabinet/build.mjs`, each with and without `--light`: `git status --short` shows no change to any built page (they use `T.prism`; none has a repeated vertex).

Not verified: browser rendering of a figure containing such a prism (no figure uses a repeated vertex); a polygon that collapses to fewer than 3 distinct points now returns those points instead of NaN, which I did not test further.

## Checks

title: turn-audit: sample clips through their final instant, not past it
body:
## What this changes

`samplesOf` in `kit/turn-audit.mjs` (now exported so it can be tested) rounds the frame count up for a non-periodic clip and clamps the last sample to the end of the clip. Periodic sweeps, and clips whose length is a whole number of frames, give the same samples as before.

## Why

The 3D turn audit takes the states for its order, posed and continuity checks from `samplesOf`. It rounded the count, so a clip whose length is not a whole number of frames was either sampled past its end or never sampled at its last pose. On current main (`bc943e4`), with `samplesOf` exported:

    samplesOf({from:0,to:1,periodic:false}, 0.4)    // [0, 0.4, 0.8, 1.2000000000000002]   past the end
    samplesOf({from:0,to:1,periodic:false}, 0.3)    // [0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.8999999999999999]   never reaches 1
    samplesOf({from:0,to:0,periodic:false}, 1/60)   // two samples, the second past `to`

In practice a clip such as `{ from: 0, to: 0.42, frame: 1/60 }` ended its check at 0.4167 s, so the settled final pose, where a part that overshoots or collides would show, was never audited; `--quick` multiplies the frame and widens the gap. Poses past `to` also reach `family.at(x)` outside the range the clip defines.

## Verification

New `scripts/turn-audit-samples.test.mjs` (4 tests: first sample is `from`, last is `to`, strictly increasing, never past `to`, gaps no wider than a frame; whole-frame clips keep their frames, e.g. 61 samples for 0..1 at 1/60; an empty clip gives one sample; periodic sweeps still stop one frame short of the repeat).

- main (with only `export` added so the test can import it): `# pass 2 / # fail 2`
- with the change: `# pass 4 / # fail 0`
- `node examples/turning-dial/build.mjs --audit --quick` ends `turn audit failed: 4 problems (quick run, undersampled: the full run is the proof)` with identical counts on main and on this branch (755 states with swaps, 1993 order states, 455 posed states); its clips (`0..4` and `0..2.2` at 1/60) are whole frames, so they are sampled as before. I did not look into those 4 problems; they are the same without this change.

Not verified: the full (non `--quick`) turn audit run; a figure that has a clip whose length is not a whole number of frames, since the repo has none.

title: turn-build: reject star polygons as non-convex prisms
body:
## What this changes

`convexOrThrow` in `kit/turn-build.mjs` (the check `T.prism` runs on every ring) also requires the turning angles around the ring to add up to one full turn, and ignores repeated vertices while it measures.

## Why

The check only compared the sign of each turn. A star polygon (pentagram, heptagram) turns the same way at every vertex but winds twice, so it passed as a convex part and reached the collision, sort and silhouette code, which assume convexity. On current main (`bc943e4`):

    T.prism({ name: "star", F, s0: 0, s1: 2, polygon: <pentagram, 5 points, r=3> })   // accepted, ring n = 5
    T.prism({ polygon: <bowtie> })  // throws "part is not convex; split it into convex pieces"
    T.prism({ polygon: <L shape> }) // throws the same

A star now throws the same message the other non-convex shapes already get.

## Verification

New `scripts/turn-convex-check.test.mjs` (5 tests: pentagram and heptagram, both windings, are rejected; bowtie and L stay rejected; triangles, a pentagon, a 12-gon, a reversed hexagon, a polygon with a collinear point and a rounded rectangle stay accepted; a closed polygon with a repeated vertex stays accepted).

title: fix: a headless screenshot can miss the WebGL canvas, and there was no way to see one
body:
## The problem

`kit/gl.mjs` creates its context with `preserveDrawingBuffer: false`, so `capture.mjs` and every `["shot", …]` of a shader page come back **with the canvas missing entirely**. `references/webgl.md` claimed the opposite ("`capture.mjs` also has WebGL now, so it is fine for still shots of a shader page"), which is what made this expensive to rediscover: I spent several rounds concluding "the shader is not drawing" when a `readPixels` in the same frame showed 97,000 lit pixels in a region the screenshot showed as empty background.

The existing guidance ("readback only works in the same task as the draw") is correct, but it left no way to *see* the result, so the shape, the colour ramp and a cut at the canvas edge were all unverifiable by eye.

## What this adds

```
node scripts/grab-canvas.mjs page.html --actions '[["key","End"],["wait",900]]' --out plume.png
node scripts/grab-canvas.mjs page.html --actions '…' --probe
```

- reads the buffer back inside a `requestAnimationFrame`, so it is the same task as the draw
- crops and scales **inside the page** until the encoded PNG fits on one line, because a long `eval` result gets truncated in transit and still looks like a PNG
- verifies the IDAT stream inflates and **refuses to save a truncated file**
- `--probe` prints the checklist numbers: `lit`, `edge` (must be 0), `meanColour`, `meanAlpha`, `p95`, `maxAlpha`, `maxColour`

## The metric correction

Under premultiplied alpha the colour channels do not say how bright something looks — a pale grey veil at alpha 4 measures `meanColour ≈ 1`, and a black card at alpha 255 measures 0. This is stated now as a rule: judge the dark build on `meanColour`, the light build on `meanAlpha`.

## Also

`references/kit.md` gains a **Silent failures** table for four traps that produce no error and only a wrong picture:

| Trap | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `tube(..., { gaps })` takes a **flat** list of `[lo, hi]` pairs | a nested pair destructures to arrays, `Math.min` returns `NaN`, the gap is dropped and the tube still passes through what it was meant to clear |
| `settle(obj, goal, dt, tau)` with `tau << dt` | the spring diverges; one frame later the value is `1e69` and whatever it drives has left the building |
| `glCamera(P)` returns only `{ origin, k, cam }` | there is no right vector to read; derive `[cos a, -sin a, 0]` from the azimuth |
| audit screen coordinates are **viewBox** units | the card's CSS box is often not its viewBox size, so a reported position points at the wrong part of the drawing |

No geometry, no kit behaviour and no public API change: two new scripts, one corrected paragraph, one new table.

Verified on a real shader figure: `--probe` reports `edge: 0` with the expected peak, and `--out` writes a PNG that inflates cleanly and shows what the screenshot could not.

body:
## What this changes

`capture.mjs`, `drive.mjs` and `turn-check.mjs` now open only local files and `localhost` by default. Any other http(s) host is refused with exit code 2 unless `--allow-remote` is passed. `--allow-file-access-from-files` is passed to Chrome only when the page is a local file. The decision lives in one new module, `scripts/safe-target.mjs`, with `scripts/safe-target.test.mjs`.

## Why

`drive.mjs` can run JavaScript in the page it opens (`eval`, `until`) and clicks and types into it. Pointing it at a remote URL, for example one pasted into a prompt, runs that page's code next to a debugging port, and the file-access flag was on for every page. Local pages and dev servers behave as before.

A separate observation, not changed here: on Linux the scripts always pass `--no-sandbox`. That is convenient in containers, but it also turns the sandbox off for every page on a normal desktop. An opt-in might be worth considering.

## Checks

- [x] No comments in code.
- [x] Kit untouched; no example changes.
- [x] `node --test scripts/safe-target.test.mjs scripts/capture.test.mjs scripts/drive.test.mjs scripts/navigation.test.mjs scripts/chrome-startup.test.mjs scripts/session.test.mjs`: 25 pass, 0 fail.
- [x] `node scripts/capture.mjs https://example.com` exits 2 with a clear message.
- [x] A line under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`.
- [ ] Not run: the full CI matrix, and the 3D `turn-check` path against a live page.

## Screenshots

None: scripts only, no visual change.

title: turn-audit: bound continuity and order steps to actual motion intervals
body:
## What this changes

- Updates `continuity` in `kit/turn-audit.mjs` so each clip step records its actual `[prevX, x]` start and `dx = x - prevX` instead of `[x - frameOf(family), x]` with `dx = frameOf(family)`.
- Updates `continuity` group sweeps (`turn`, `hinge`, `slide`) in `kit/turn-audit.mjs` to step via `samplesOf({ from: sweep.from, to: sweep.to, periodic: false }, delta).slice(1)` and track `prevX` and `dx = x - prevX` across both `compare` and `measures`.
- Filters `order` swap event probes on non-periodic clips to stay within `[family.from, family.to]`.
- Adds regression tests in `scripts/turn-audit-samples.test.mjs` covering short and partial-frame clip bounds, discontinuity detection in a clip's final partial frame, and non-integer/zero-span `hinge` and `slide` sweeps.

## Why

After PR #74 updated `samplesOf(family, frame)` to clamp the final sample of a non-periodic clip to `family.to`, three step-interval bugs remained in `kit/turn-audit.mjs`:

1. **Clip continuity step mismatch and missed final-frame discontinuities**: `continuity` still pushed `{ x: x - frameOf(family), dx: frameOf(family) }` into `clipSteps`. Whenever a clip's duration `to - from` was not a whole multiple of `frameOf(family)`:
   - On a clip shorter than one frame (`to - from < frameOf(family)`), `x - frameOf(family) < family.from`, causing `halving` to evaluate `family.at(t)` at timestamps before `family.from`.
   - On a multi-frame clip ending in a partial frame `[prevX, to]`, `halving` subdivided `[to - frame, to]` (overlapping the previous frame `[to - frame, prevX]`) instead of `[prevX, to]`, reporting `at: to - frame` instead of `prevX` — and if the clip moved through `to - frame -> prevX` and then jumped back to the `to - frame` pose during `[prevX, to]`, `halving` compared identical endpoints (`full === 0`) and silently missed the discontinuity.
2. **Group sweep overshoot/undershoot on `hinge` and `slide` groups**: `continuity` still computed `count = Math.max(1, Math.round(span / delta))` and stepped to `sweep.from + c * delta`. Stationary `hinge` (`range: [a, a]`) or `slide` (`travel: 0`) groups stepped outside their range to `from + delta`, and non-integer-step `hinge` or short `slide` ranges either stepped past `sweep.to` or stopped short of `sweep.to`.
3. **Out-of-bounds `order` event probes**: When a depth-order swap occurred on the first or last step of a non-periodic clip, `c.x ± delta` could probe outside `[family.from, family.to]`.

## Checks

Tick what applies, and say why for anything left unticked.

- [x] Every example rebuilds, and `git status --short` shows only the changes I meant.
- [x] No comments in code.
- [x] Kit changes are opt-in, and every existing example is byte-identical (or this PR says which pages change and why).
- [ ] I built and looked at both themes. *(Not applicable: this PR only modifies `kit/turn-audit.mjs` and tests; no example figure or theme styling is changed, and all 14 built example HTML files remain byte-identical.)*
- [x] Figures with pipes, cables or round parts: `node build.mjs --audit` ends `audit passed`, every failing line at 0.
- [ ] `node scripts/lines.mjs` prints `line ends: 0` on both themes and in every resting pose. *(Not applicable: no SVG line drawing or example figure output is modified.)*
- [ ] Shaders: a slowed contact sheet across every transition shows no pop, and `--no-webgl` still reads. *(Not applicable: no shaders or WebGL code touched.)*
- [x] 3D: a full run ends `turn audit passed`, and `scripts/turn-check.mjs` passes.
- [x] Every number in the figure, the readout, the caption and the docs is true.
- [x] A line under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Screenshots

Not applicable — this change is in `kit/turn-audit.mjs` and all 14 example pages rebuild byte-identically (`git diff --exit-code examples/`).

title: Fix T.split detail and plane partitioning across split halves
body:
## What

Fixes `T.split` in `kit/turn-build.mjs` so that splitting a `T.prism` or `T.round` partitions its `details` (`seams`, `dots`, `bolts`, `rings`, `rules`, `ribs`) and any attached `T.plane` / `T.billboard` planes across the `.a` and `.b` halves instead of dropping details on `.b`, leaving out-of-span details floating past the cut on `.a`, or wiping `seams` on upright `T.round` parts.

### Problem

When `T.split(part, { n, d })` splits a `prism` or `round` so that both halves participate in Painter's sorting:

1. **Default upright `T.round` wiped `seams` before `T.split` could read them**:
   In `T.round`, the default upright path (`fixed !== false && Math.abs(F.a[0]) < 1e-6 && Math.abs(F.a[1]) < 1e-6`) baked `seams` into the static 2D SVG and passed `details: { ...(options.details ?? {}), ribs, seams: undefined }` to `T.fixed`. Because `part.details.seams` became `undefined` and `part.round` did not store the original `options.details`, calling `T.split` on an upright round lost all `seams` on both `.a` and `.b`.
2. **`T.split` on a `round` dropped all `details` on `.b` and left `.b`'s details on `.a`**:
   `T.split` constructed `.a` (`[s0, sCut]`) with unfiltered `details: part.details` and constructed `.b` (`[sCut, s1]`) with **no `details` argument at all**. As a result:
   - `.b` lost all `seams`, `bolts`, `dots`, `rings`, `rules`, and `ribs` located in `(sCut, s1]`.
   - `.a` kept `seams` in `(sCut, s1]`, which the browser runtime drew as floating seam rings in empty air beyond `.a`'s cut end (`sCut`), and `detailParts` emitted duplicate child parts (`bolt`, `dot`, `rib`) for `.b`'s span under `.a.*` names.
3. **`T.split` on a `prism` across its axis (`|n · F.a| ≈ 1`) duplicated out-of-span `seams` and dropped `.b`'s `dots`**:
   - Both `.a` (`[s0, sCut]`) and `.b` (`[sCut, s1]`) received the full unfiltered `details.seams` array, so `.a` drew seams belonging to `(sCut, s1]` floating past `sCut` and `.b` drew seams belonging to `[s0, sCut)` floating before `sCut`.
   - `.a` kept all `dots` (including those in `(sCut, s1]`) while `.b` had `dots` forced to `[]`.
4. **`T.split` on a `prism` along its axis (`n · F.a ≈ 0`) gave all `dots` to `.a` and dropped attached `T.plane` / `T.billboard` planes**:
   - `.a` kept all `dots` even when a dot's `(u, v)` coordinates lay on `.b`'s side of the cut plane, while `.b` received `dots: []`.
   - Any planes added via `T.plane(part, ...)` or `T.billboard(part, ...)` before `T.split(part, ...)` were left on the dead `part` (`part.dead = true`) and omitted from `TURN.emit()`.

### Fix

1. Preserve `details: options.details ?? {}` on `part.round` in `T.round` so splitting a default upright round reads the original `seams` and `ribs` specification.
2. Add `axialDetails(details, a0, a1, second)` in `kit/turn-build.mjs` to partition axial details across `[s0, sCut]` (`second = false`, inclusive of `sCut`) and `[sCut, s1]` (`second = true`, strictly above `sCut`):
   - Filters `seams`, `dots`, `bolts`, `rings`, and `rules` to each half's axial span.
   - Clips `ribs` (`[rs.s0, rs.s1]`) to `[a0, a1]`, linearly interpolating `r0`/`r1` when present and preserving boundary `seams` (`true`, `"first"`, `"last"`, `false`) only at unclipped ends.
3. Partition `dots` by cut-plane side (`side([dot.at[1], dot.at[2]]) <= 1e-6` vs `> 1e-6`) when splitting a `prism` along its axis, while keeping axial `seams` on both halves.
4. Partition custom `T.plane` / `T.billboard` planes attached to `part` onto `.a` or `.b` according to which side of the split plane each plane's world origin lies on.

### Validation

- Added `scripts/turn-split-details.test.mjs` covering:
  - Splitting a `T.prism` across its axis (partitioning `seams`, `dots`, and attached `T.plane`s across `.a` and `.b` and verifying `TURN.emit()`).
  - Splitting a `T.prism` along its axis (partitioning `dots` and attached `T.plane`s across the cut plane while preserving `seams` on both halves).
  - Splitting both a live (`fixed: false`) and a default upright `T.round` (including recursive splits) and verifying that `seams`, `bolts`, `dots`, `rings`, `rules`, `ribs` (with clipped spans, interpolated radii, and boundary seams), and custom `T.plane`s are partitioned cleanly without duplicates or dropped details.
- Ran `node --test scripts/turn-split-details.test.mjs scripts/turn-split-owner.test.mjs scripts/turn-prism-corners.test.mjs scripts/turn-prism-polygon.test.mjs` — all pass.
- Rebuilt all 14 examples (`for f in examples/*/build.mjs; do node "$f"; done`) and verified `git diff --exit-code examples/`.

## Checks

- [x] Read `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- [x] If `kit/` or `SKILL.md` changed, every `examples/*/build.mjs` was re-run and the rebuilt HTML is in this branch.
- [x] If a figure is included or changed, `node scripts/audit.mjs <figure>.html` passes with zero errors and both themes were checked with `scripts/capture.mjs`.
- [x] No comments in code.
- [x] Line added under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md` (unless this is a typo or grammar fix).

title: Thoughts on next steps: graduating the canvas painter, multi-level zoom primitives, and faster 3D orbit audits
body:
### What are you asking for?

Something else

### The idea

First, thank you for building and open-sourcing Anatomy, the "object is the explanation" philosophy, the zero-dependency kit, and the uncompromising verification suite (`audit.mjs`, `turn-audit.mjs`, `lines.mjs`) make this one of the most thoughtfully engineered agent skills out there.
After reading through the kit, references, recent PRs, and the experimental modules in `kit/` (`turn-fixed.mjs`, `canvas-painter.mjs`, and `gl-shared.mjs`), I wanted to open a discussion on a few directions that seem to build naturally on where the project is heading, and ask which of these (if any) align with your goals:
1. **Graduating `turn-fixed.mjs`, `canvas-painter.mjs`, and `gl-shared.mjs` for dense 3D scenes**
   - `references/3d.md` notes the main-thread SVG DOM bottleneck on dense scenes like `turning-dial/stress.mjs` (380 parts at ~20 fps desktop / 13–15 fps mobile).
   - The experimental `t3Arena` binary float tokens, `shift: true` translation fast-path in `turn-fixed.mjs`, and dirty-rect 2D canvas renderer in `canvas-painter.mjs` (with `controller.snapshot()` / `exportSvg()` preserving DOM SVG output when needed) look like a very clean solution.
   - Are you planning to fold `painter: "canvas"` and `shift: true` into `kit/turn.mjs` as opt-in mount options once they pass `turn-check.mjs` (`--fidelity`, `--order`, `--pops`, `--lines`), or are there specific edge cases still holding them back?
2. **Connecting stage zoom (`canvas-painter` / `gl-shared`) with the `levels=n` reference figure (#51)**
   - In #51, you mentioned wanting to hand-build a `computer → CPU → ALU` reference figure first and distill the rules into `references/depth.md` before adding `levels=`.
   - Noticeably, `canvas-painter.mjs` already includes `zoom(z, cx, cy)` and `gl-shared.mjs` adds `untransformed` canvas sizing.
   - When building that first multi-level reference figure, do you envision the transition between levels happening via viewBox/camera frustum interpolation (`fitProjection` lerping + parent shell cutaway/fade envelopes in SVG), or via stage-level zoom?
3. **Parallelizing `turn-audit.mjs` (`TA.orbitOrExit`) with `node:worker_threads`**
   - A full 3D orbit audit currently budgets 30–40s per part (~15–20 minutes for a 30-part figure), which often outlasts standard 10-minute agent tool timeouts, while `--quick` can miss narrow `continuity` failures.
   - Since `posed`, `routes`, and the 4×/16× halving rasterizer in `continuity` evaluate independent angle/step intervals, sharding them across Node's built-in `node:worker_threads` could cut full-audit wall-clock time by 4–6× while remaining 100% deterministic and zero-dependency. Would a worker-pool opt-in (or default) in `turn-audit.mjs` be welcome?
4. **Lightweight verification harness for React/Next.js figures**
   - Currently, `examples/test-rig/` and `examples/spot-plate/` don't have build scripts in CI, and React figures can't be run through `lines.mjs` / `capture.mjs` directly or submitted via `publish.mjs`.
   - Since CI already installs `react`, `react-dom`, `typescript`, and `esbuild` in a temp directory for the React unit tests, would you be interested in a small opt-in script that wraps a React figure into a standalone HTML page so agents can run the standard browser checks (`capture`, `lines`, `drive`) on TSX figures too?
5. **Small multi-agent parity touch-ups in `publish.mjs` / `session.mjs`**
   - Following #81 (MiniMax Code support), `AGENTS` in `scripts/publish.mjs` and `references/publish.md` still only list `Claude Code`, `OpenCode`, `Codex`, `Antigravity`, and `Other`.
   - Also, `scripts/session.mjs` currently reads time/token metrics exclusively from Claude Code's `~/.claude/projects` logs. Would you be open to adding `"MiniMax Code"` to `publish.mjs` and supporting session log parsers for the other documented agents where their local transcript format is stable?

### Kind of figure

Not about a figure

### Why it is worth adding

Each of these aims to reinforce Anatomy's existing strengths, keeping the kit zero-dependency and existing examples byte-identical, while removing practical friction around 3D frame rates on dense figures, 15+ minute full orbit audits inside agent sessions, and verification parity across React figures and non-Claude agents.

I completely understand if some of these are already in progress privately or intentionally out of scope. I'd love to hear your thoughts on which of these align with your vision and would be most useful to prototype or contribute PRs for.

### What you tried instead

Reviewed the current `kit/` implementation (`turn.mjs` vs. `turn-fixed.mjs`, `canvas-painter.mjs`, `gl-shared.mjs`, `turn-audit.mjs`), `references/3d.md`, `scripts/publish.mjs`, and open issues/PRs (#51, #52, #78–#84).

### Before you submit

- [x] I searched the existing issues.
- [x] I read the Limits section of the README.

title: audit: bound elliptical arcs in markupBox
body:
## What this changes

`markupBox` (kit/audit.mjs) now bounds elliptical arcs (`A`/`a`) through their centre form instead of using only the endpoint, and reads arc flags written without separators (`a5 5 0 1010 0`, valid SVG and common in minified paths).

## Why

`M0 0A5 5 0 0 1 10 0` is a semicircle 5 tall, but `markupBox` returned `[0,0,10,0]`, and `M0 0a5 5 0 1010 0` returned `[0,0,0,0]` because `1010` was read as one number. `markupBox` feeds `T.fixed` (`spec.box`, which the never-overlap pairing rules compare) and `coverage`, so a part drawn with arcs was measured as a flat line.

Native check (headless Chrome through `scripts/drive.mjs`, `getBBox`) against the new `markupBox`:

| path | native `getBBox` | `markupBox` before | `markupBox` after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `M20 50A10 10 0 1 1 30 50` | 15, 31.34, 35, 50 | 20, 50, 30, 50 | 15, 31.34, 35, 50 |
| `M0 0a5 5 0 1010 0` at translate(40 40) | 0, 0, 10, 5 (local) | 40, 40, 40, 40 | 40, 40, 50, 45 |
| `M0 0A10 2 90 0 1 4 0` at translate(60 60) | 0, -10, 4, 0 (local) | 60, 60, 64, 60 | 60, 50, 64, 60 |

## Checks

- [x] Every example rebuilds, and `git status --short` shows only the changes I meant. Rebuilt dark and light: dial-indicator, desk-computer, arcade-cabinet, ripple-tank, turning-dial (no diff). NOT rebuilt: raptor-engine, spot-plate, test-rig (none of the examples' sources call `coverage`, `T.fixed` or `markupBox`, checked with grep).
- [x] No comments in code.
- [x] Kit changes are opt-in, and every existing example is byte-identical. Only paths containing `A`/`a` change result; the rebuilt examples are identical.
- [ ] I built and looked at both themes. Not applicable: no figure changes.
- [ ] Audit / lines / shaders / 3D checks. Not applicable: no figure or shader change; the full audit of raptor-engine was not run.
- [x] A line under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`.

Tests: new `scripts/audit-path-arcs.test.mjs` (10 cases, analytic expected boxes, no browser). Before the change `node --test scripts/audit-path-arcs.test.mjs` gives `# pass 1 # fail 9`; after, `# pass 10 # fail 0`. Existing `audit-affine-bounds`, `audit-path-origin`, `audit-svg-attributes`, `audit-empty-clipping` still pass (`# pass 39 # fail 0`, concurrency 1).

Known limit: arcs are sampled every 0.25 degrees (so a transformed arc stays correct under any affine matrix), which is within about 0.001 units for radii up to 100.

## Screenshots

None; no visual change.

title: audit: include reflected control points of smooth curves in markupBox
body:
## What this changes

`markupBox` (kit/audit.mjs) now includes the implied first control point of smooth curve commands: `S`/`s` after a `C`/`S`, and `T`/`t` after a `Q`/`T` (the reflection of the previous control point about the current point). Like the explicit control points it already takes, this keeps the box a superset of the drawn curve.

## Why

The path scanner pushed only the explicit points of `S`/`T`, so the box of a path built from smooth commands could stop short of the curve. Measured with headless Chrome `getBBox` (through `scripts/drive.mjs`) against `markupBox` before this change:

| path | native `getBBox` | `markupBox` before | `markupBox` after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `M0 0C0 10 10 10 10 0S20 0 20 0` | 0, -4.44, 20, 7.5 | 0, 0, 20, 10 (curve leaves the box) | 0, -10, 20, 10 |
| `M0 0Q5 10 10 0T20 0` | 0, -5, 20, 5 | 0, 0, 20, 10 (curve leaves the box) | 0, -10, 20, 10 |

`markupBox` feeds `T.fixed` (`spec.box`, compared by the never-overlap pairing rules) and `coverage`. The new box is the control-point hull, the same convention as for explicit `C`/`Q`, not a tight fit; an `S`/`T` that follows a line or another command gets no reflection, as in the SVG spec.

## Checks

- [x] Every example rebuilds, and `git status --short` shows only the changes I meant. Rebuilt dark and light: turning-dial, dial-indicator, desk-computer (no diff). NOT rebuilt: arcade-cabinet, ripple-tank, raptor-engine, spot-plate, test-rig; no example source calls `coverage`, `T.fixed` or `markupBox` (checked with grep).
- [x] No comments in code.
- [x] Kit changes are opt-in. Only paths containing `S`/`s`/`T`/`t` change result.
- [ ] Both themes / audit / lines / shaders / 3D checks: not applicable, no figure or shader change; the raptor-engine audit was not run.
- [x] A line under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`.

Tests: new `scripts/audit-path-smooth.test.mjs` (7 cases: the native boxes above, plus relative forms, chained `T`, and `S`/`T` after a line, which must not reflect; native values were measured in Chrome and are hard coded, so the test needs no browser). Before the change: `# pass 2 # fail 5`. After: `# pass 7 # fail 0`. Existing `audit-affine-bounds`, `audit-path-origin`, `audit-svg-attributes`, `audit-empty-clipping`: `# pass 39 # fail 0` (concurrency 1).

Note: this touches the same function as #86 (arc bounds) in a different hunk.

## Screenshots

None; no visual change.

title: publish.mjs rejects "MiniMax Code" as --agent, although MiniMax Code is now a supported agent
body:
## What happens

Commit 0e3ace9 ("Add MiniMax Code support alongside Claude Code, Antigravity, OpenCode and Codex") added MiniMax Code to the README, CONTRIBUTING.md, SKILL.md front matter, the CHANGELOG and the bug-report form, but not to the `--agent` whitelist in `scripts/publish.mjs`. A MiniMax Code user who tries to publish a figure to the community gallery is rejected:

```
$ node scripts/publish.mjs <figure folder> --into <anatomy-community clone> \
    --id my-figure --title "..." --prompt "..." --author <user> --agent "MiniMax Code" \
    --model "..." --minutes 45 --tokens 380k --no-session

publish: --agent must be one of: Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Antigravity, Other
```

Exit code 1, nothing published. The only workarounds are to record the wrong agent or fall back to `Other`.

## Evidence

- `scripts/publish.mjs:12` — `const AGENTS = ["Claude Code", "OpenCode", "Codex", "Antigravity", "Other"];` (no "MiniMax Code")
- `scripts/publish.mjs:74` — `if (!AGENTS.includes(options.agent)) usage(...)` rejects it
- `references/publish.md:21` — the documented usage line still reads `[--agent "Claude Code"|OpenCode|Codex|Antigravity|Other]`
- Compare the docs added in 0e3ace9: `README.md:3`, `README.md:51`, `SKILL.md:5` and `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml:32` all list MiniMax Code as a supported agent.

## Expected

`--agent "MiniMax Code"` is accepted and recorded in `figure.json`, since every other surface in the repo advertises MiniMax Code as a supported agent. The publish flow (`references/publish.md` step 4) is the only place the agent is actually recorded, so right now a MiniMax Code figure cannot be published under its real agent name.

## Fix direction

Add `"MiniMax Code"` to the `AGENTS` array in `scripts/publish.mjs:12` and to the usage text in `scripts/publish.mjs` (`usage()`), and update the `[--agent ...]` line in `references/publish.md:21` to match. A one-line test in `scripts/publish.test.mjs` asserting `--agent "MiniMax Code"` is accepted would keep the whitelist in sync with the docs.

title: publish.mjs --pages silently drops a page when two listed pages share the same theme
body:
## What happens

`detectPages` keys explicitly listed pages by their `data-theme`. Two pages with the same theme collide on the same key, and the second assignment silently overwrites the first. The dropped page is then treated as an ordinary source file: it is copied into `src/`, committed, never built and never listed in `figure.json`.

`scripts/publish.mjs:98`:

```js
for (const page of named) pages[themeOf(source, page) === "light" ? "light" : themeOf(source, page) === "dark" ? "dark" : slug(page)] = page;
```

If `--pages main.html,alt.html` and both files have `data-theme="dark"`, `pages` ends up `{ dark: "alt.html" }` — `main.html` is gone as a page.

## Repro

Minimal figure folder (`build.mjs` present, both pages pre-built):

```
src/main.html  -> <!doctype html><body data-theme="dark">...
src/alt.html   -> <!doctype html><body data-theme="dark">...
```

`publish({ source, into, id, title, prompt, author, pages: ["main.html", "alt.html"], ... })` produces:

- `figure.pages` = `{ "dark": "src/alt.html" }` — only one of the two requested pages
- `figure.build` = `[[\"src/build.mjs\"]]` — one build command, no light page
- `main.html` is copied into `figures/<author>/<id>/src/` as a plain source file (it is not in the `outputs` set, `scripts/publish.mjs:163`), so it ships in the PR but is never referenced by `figure.json`

I verified this by calling `publish()` with those options: the returned `figure` object records only `alt.html`.

As a second-order effect, because the surviving page is treated as a build output and is excluded from the copied source (`scripts/publish.mjs:163-164`), `pageText` reads it from `dest/src` after the build (`scripts/publish.mjs:213`) — a figure whose build script does not emit that exact page name fails with `ENOENT: no such file or directory ... /src/alt.html` instead of any message about the theme collision.

## Expected

`--pages` exists precisely for figures the auto-detection cannot resolve, i.e. non-standard page sets (the slug fallback at the end of line 98 already handles a third, non-light/dark page). Two extra views sharing a theme (e.g. `overview.html` + `exploded.html`, both dark) should either both be recorded under distinct keys or be rejected with an error naming both pages. Silently publishing a figure that is missing half its requested pages is the worst outcome: the gallery shows one page and the other ships dead in the repo.

## Fix direction

Detect the collision when building `pages`: if the theme key is already taken, fall back to the filename slug used for non-light/dark pages (so `main.html` would land under its own key), or throw `two pages share the "dark" theme: main.html, alt.html — give them distinct data-theme values`. A regression test in `scripts/publish.test.mjs` with a two-same-theme fixture would cover it.

title: turn-check.mjs: reject option values it cannot use
body:
## What this changes

`turn-check.mjs` validates `--angles`, `--width`, `--height`, `--scale` and `--throttle` before it builds the figure or starts Chrome, with one message naming the flag (`--step` and `--fine` already did this). It adds `scripts/turn-check-options.test.mjs` and a line under `Unreleased`.

## Why

Evidence on current `main`:


## What this changes

`lines.mjs` validates its own options before it hands off to `drive.mjs`: `--tolerance` and `--wait` must be numbers of 0 or more, and `--out`, `--select`, `--tolerance`, `--wait` must have a value that is not another flag. Adds `scripts/lines-options.test.mjs` and a line under `Unreleased`.

## Why

`take` returns `argv[at + 1]` unchecked and the numbers go through `Number()`. Building the actions on current `main` (with a stub standing in for `drive.mjs` that prints what it receives):

```
lines.mjs fig.html --tolerance abc      -> [["wait",1500],["lines",null,null,{"tolerance":null}]]
lines.mjs fig.html --wait abc           -> [["wait",null],["lines",null,null,{"tolerance":1}]]
lines.mjs fig.html --out --tolerance 2  -> [["wait",1500],["lines","--tolerance",null,{"tolerance":1}]]  (+ stray "2")
```

title: drive.mjs: validate wait, slow, move, click, drag, key, until and eval arguments
body:
## What this changes

`drive.mjs` already checks `orbit` and `sheet` arguments before Chrome starts (#67). This extends that check to `wait`, `slow`, `move`, `click`, `drag`, `key`, `until` and `eval`, with one message naming the action. Adds `scripts/drive-action-values.test.mjs` and a line under `Unreleased`.

## Why

Read from current `main`:

- `["wait", "soon"]` calls `sleep(NaN)`; `setTimeout(done, NaN)` fires after 1 ms (checked in Node: `NaN wait fired after 1 ms`), so a mistyped wait is silently skipped.
- `["slow", 0]` or `["slow", "slow"]` sets `window.__driveSpeed` to 0 / `NaN`; the virtual clock then never advances (or becomes `NaN`) and the page animation stops.
- `["move", sel]` / `["drag", sel, ...]` with missing fractions send `NaN` mouse coordinates to `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`.
- `["key"]` reaches `key.length` on `undefined` in the `key` action, partway through a run.

After the change all of these exit 1 with e.g. `wait needs milliseconds of 0 or more, got soon`, before Chrome starts. The documented forms (`["click", sel]`, `["click", sel, fx, fy]`, `["key", "Enter", null, "NumpadEnter"]`, `["until", js]`, `["until", js, ms]`, `["drag", ..., steps]`, and so on) are covered by a second test and still pass validation. I also grepped `SKILL.md`, `references/`, `README.md` and the existing tests for action forms; none of them are rejected.

title: turn-audit: add opt-in worker_threads parallelism (--workers)
body:
## What this changes

Implements Roadmap Item #3 from #85: opt-in `node:worker_threads` parallelism for the 3D orbit audit (`kit/turn-audit.mjs`).

- **`orbit(T, R, P, { ..., workers })`**: Accepts `workers: true` (`os.availableParallelism()`) or a positive integer worker count (default `false` / single-threaded). Keeps `orbit` and `orbitOrExit` synchronous via a `node:worker_threads` pool coordinated with `SharedArrayBuffer`, `Atomics.wait` and `receiveMessageOnPort`.
- **`orbitOrExit(T, R, P, options)`**: Reads `--workers` (`true`) or `--workers=N` / `--workers N` from `argv` when `options.workers` is not explicitly set.
- **Exact single-threaded parity**:
  - `order`: Workers evaluate `TURN.emit` and stateless per-layer checks (`framed`, `groupPairs`, cross-group GJK margins and Kahn cycle detection) in batches, while `TURN.order` runs sequentially on the main thread in exact state order so stateful `previous` tie-breaking, `layer.rel` warm-starts and swap overlap areas match 100%.
  - `posed`: Contiguous state slices are evaluated across workers and merged in chunk order through the main thread's `posedSeen` set.
  - `continuity`: Group sweeps are partitioned into contiguous step ranges `[cStart..cEnd]` (each seeded at `cStart - 1`), and `halving` candidates (both group measures and clip steps) are evaluated in parallel worker batches.
  - `depth`: Workers compute `evalOrderState` and `A.overlapsOf` ray-cast grids in parallel while the main thread compares pairs against `state.orders` in exact order.
- **Tests & Docs**:
  - Added `scripts/turn-audit-workers.test.mjs` verifying deep equality of `orbit(...)` results, `orbitReport(...)` output, `log` callback ordering, deterministic fault reporting, `--workers` CLI parsing and invalid worker count rejection.
  - Updated `references/3d.md`, `references/kit.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
  - Structured to apply cleanly alongside #83 with zero merge conflicts.

## Why

Full 3D orbit audits can exceed agent shell timeouts on multi-group figures (#85). Offloading the stateless per-pose geometry, rasterization and ray-casting work across worker threads cuts wall-clock time by ~3×–4× while keeping results 100% identical to the single-threaded run.

### Benchmarks & Parity (10-core Apple Silicon)

| Command | Single-threaded | `--workers` | Speedup | Report diff (excluding elapsed seconds) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `node examples/turning-dial/build.mjs --light --audit` (full: 9,109 order states, 3,254 posed states, 800 halving, 72 depth states) | 452.24 s | 115.48 s | **3.92×** | 0 lines (`diff -u` identical) |
| `node examples/turning-dial/build.mjs --light --audit --quick` | 43.01 s | 13.51 s | **3.18×** | 0 lines (`diff -u` identical) |
| `node examples/turning-dial/stress.mjs --light --audit --quick` | 70.07 s | 25.42 s | **2.76×** | 0 lines (`diff -u` identical) |

title: Add opt-in scripts/react-page.mjs harness for React/Next.js figures
body:
## What this changes

Adds an opt-in standalone page wrapper (`scripts/react-page.mjs`) and test suite (`scripts/react-page.test.mjs`) for React/Next.js figures, with zero dependencies added to `kit/` or the repository (follow-up to #85, item 4).

- **`scripts/react-page.mjs <figure-dir | file.tsx>`:**
  - Resolves `react`, `react-dom`, and `esbuild` from the project's `node_modules` or `NODE_PATH` (matching CI's temporary test environment).
  - Bundles and server-renders the resting pose via `renderToString` and hydrates it on the client with `hydrateRoot(..., { onRecoverableError: (e) => console.error(e) })` so hydration mismatches fail `capture.mjs` / `drive.mjs` console checks.
  - Wraps the figure with `pageHtml` from `kit/iso-kit.mjs`, inlines `ISO_CSS` plus any `.css` files imported by the figure (`rig.css`, `spot-plate.css`, etc., deduplicating `iso.css`), and supports `--light`, `--theme dark|light`, `--out <file.html>`, `--export <ComponentName>`, `--title`, `--width`, and `--css`.
  - Resolves Next.js `@/` and `~/` path aliases from `tsconfig.json` / `jsconfig.json` (or project root), and automatically falls back to `kit/` for `@/components/iso/...` or `components/iso/...` imports when a figure has not yet copied `kit/` into its host project.
  - Instruments `"use client"` component boundaries during SSR to automatically detect and report the two large-page React Server Component traps documented in `references/react.md`:
    1. A React element prop passed from a Server Component to a `"use client"` component without a root `key`.
    2. A `"use client"` component nested inside a server-built element prop.
- **`scripts/react-page.test.mjs`:**
  - Builds `examples/test-rig` and `examples/spot-plate` in both dark and light themes and drives them in headless Chrome via `scripts/drive.mjs` (verifying SSR + hydration, keyboard and range-input interactions, readout updates, and `console: clean`).
  - Tests Next.js `@/components/iso/*` alias resolution and verifies that both `"use client"` boundary traps are caught and reported.
- **Docs & Changelog:** Updated `references/react.md`, `references/kit.md`, `SKILL.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Why

React/Next.js figures (`examples/test-rig/`, `examples/spot-plate/`, or figures authored in a Next.js repo) previously couldn't be run directly through `scripts/capture.mjs`, `scripts/drive.mjs`, or `scripts/lines.mjs` without spinning up an external app server, and the large-page RSC `key` warning trap (`references/react.md`) only surfaced on large streaming pages. `scripts/react-page.mjs` turns any React figure into a standalone HTML page in under a second so the standard browser checks and RSC boundary checks can run directly on TSX figures.

title: fix(turn-check): support painter: canvas pages across --order, --pops, --lines, and --perf
body:
## Summary

Implements Roadmap item 1 from #85: makes `scripts/turn-check.mjs` (`--order`, `--pops`, `--lines`, and `--perf`) work seamlessly on `painter: "canvas"` (`CANVAS2D.mount`) 3D turn figures.

### What changed

- **`scripts/turn-check.mjs`:**
  - When DOM-based checks (`--order`, `--pops`, or `--lines`) are requested on a `painter: "canvas"` page, `HELPERS` calls `C.snapshot()` and attaches any detached `<svg data-live>` layers right after their `<canvas data-canvas-live>` siblings so `getScreenCTM()`, `getBBox()`, and `document.elementsFromPoint()` work in exact stage layer order.
  - `setState(state)` routes through `window.__isoTurn.set(state)` (so `onHold()` pauses background tours) and calls `C.snapshot()` on canvas-painter pages.
  - Before `--perf` runs, `window.__tc.detachLive()` removes the temporary `<svg data-live>` layers and restores `<canvas data-canvas-live>` so `--perf` benchmarks the zero-DOM-write canvas path (`0 live elements · 0 writes and 0 moves per frame`).
- **`kit/turn-fixed.mjs`:**
  - Falls back to `stage.getBoundingClientRect()` in `unitOf()` and `angleAt()` when the first `<svg data-live>` has been detached by `CANVAS2D.mount`.
  - Guards `onFrame` during the first (`snapshotting = true`) pass of `controller.snapshot()` and preserves `controller.stats()` across `snapshot()`.
- **`scripts/turn-check-canvas.test.mjs`:**
  - Adds a `node --test` regression test verifying `--order`, `--pops`, `--lines`, and `--perf` (and their planted controls) on a `painter: "canvas"` build of `turning-dial`.

title: docs: verify captions and legends in full-figure captures
body:
## What this changes

The verification workflow now asks for a full `.iso-figure` capture at desktop and 390 px widths in both themes, using the existing `--select` option. It checks the legend and caption for clipping, overlap and agreement with the pictured state. Card crops remain the default for geometry and close-ups.

## Why

`plateHtml` and React's `Plate` place the legend and caption outside `.iso-plate`. The documented default capture therefore omits them, even though the review checklist requires a true, readable caption. A figure can pass a card-only visual review while its explanation has never appeared in a screenshot.

title: Proposal: model-synchronized explanations for interactive figures
body:
Anatomy already requires the drawing, readout, and caption to come from one model. Could we document and demonstrate an optional pattern for explanatory prose that follows the displayed state, including the motion between stops?

I built a working variant of the existing dial indicator to make this concrete before proposing a feature PR, following the issue-first contribution guide.

## Try it

- [Live light example](https://chenrui-xu.github.io/anatomy/linked-explanation/), [dark example](https://chenrui-xu.github.io/anatomy/linked-explanation-dark/), and [unchanged original light example](https://chenrui-xu.github.io/anatomy/baseline/).
- [14-second silent demonstration and overview](https://chenrui-xu.github.io/anatomy/).
- [Prototype branch](https://github.com/Chenrui-Xu/anatomy/tree/codex/linked-explanations), [implementation commit](https://github.com/Chenrui-Xu/anatomy/commit/b81d88eb8e8922ffadf08b9de6594a011526920c), and [short authoring reference](https://github.com/Chenrui-Xu/anatomy/blob/codex/linked-explanations/references/explanation.md).

![Light example with the instrument and its linked explanation](https://chenrui-xu.github.io/anatomy/light.png)

## What the example adds

Select a block and the carriage, plunger, needle, readout, and prose describe the same instant. The explanation uses the eased plunger position, not the target reading. While the instrument moves, the text says that it is settling; it does not announce the destination as an achieved result. It also distinguishes the block beneath the probe centre from contact at a block edge. Values are explicitly drawing units, not calibrated physical measurements.

The named parts link to the SVG through pointer and keyboard emphasis. There is already a useful numbered-parts/hover pattern in #58; the additional proposal here is a shared-state contract for the changing prose, together with a small reference implementation and checks.

All explanatory text remains visible. HTML part buttons support keyboard and touch; there are no extra tab stops inside the image-role SVG. Visible text can update each frame, but live announcements and the slider's accessible value update only when the mechanism settles. Reduced motion jumps to the chosen state. With scripts unavailable, the initial drawing and explanation remain readable and controls are disabled.

## Scope

The dial variant is opt-in:

```sh
node examples/dial-indicator/build.mjs --explain
node examples/dial-indicator/build.mjs --explain --light
```

The prototype includes a separate `kit/explain.mjs` candidate helper. A pure `describe(snapshot)` returns strings; `update(snapshot)` changes only the affected text nodes. The helper owns no animation loop, physics, or application state, and adds no dependencies. It is included only by the explained variant. The original drawing geometry and SVG core are unchanged.

I would be happy to start with the example and short reference alone if that is a better fit, keeping the helper local until more figures establish a useful common API. The prototype is evidence for the discussion, not a request to adopt the entire API unchanged.

## Validation so far

- All 14 new local regression tests pass: helper behavior and the actual dial's intermediate geometry/readout/prose agreement, settled announcements, block controls, keyboard stops, reduced motion, and script-free rendering.
- All 14 existing example build commands pass, and their committed HTML outputs remain byte-identical to the base commit.
- Light and dark full-figure captures were inspected at 1280 px and 390 px; the controls and text fit without horizontal overflow.
- The existing line-end check reports zero floating ends for the baseline and explained dial in both themes.

[Dark screenshot](https://chenrui-xu.github.io/anatomy/dark.png) · [Light mobile screenshot](https://chenrui-xu.github.io/anatomy/light-mobile.png) · [Dark mobile screenshot](https://chenrui-xu.github.io/anatomy/dark-mobile.png).

These checks cover this example; they do not establish that arbitrary generated explanations are factually correct or constitute a full assistive-technology audit.

Would an example-first contribution like this fit Anatomy? In particular, would you prefer the helper to remain local to the dial example for the first PR?

This grew out of work on [Mechanism Explainer](https://github.com/Chenrui-Xu/mechanism-explainer), which combines clear technical writing with interactive explanations. The proposed upstream contribution stays focused on Anatomy's existing figures and conventions.
