title: Proposal: opt-in reading annotations and notes for standalone learning pages
body:
## Proposal

Add an opt-in reading-annotations layer for long-form standalone learning pages made with Anatomy. Readers can underline, color or highlight prose, attach editable plain-text notes, and export a fresh offline HTML carrying both marks and notes.

This would be a separate starter under `assets/reading-annotations/`, loaded only when requested. Existing figures, geometry, shaders, generated examples and default skill behavior stay unchanged. Dynamic controls, SVG and MathML are excluded from persistent prose anchors.

## Behavior

- Text-selection toolbar for underline, red text, highlight, range clearing, undo and redo.
- Click or keyboard activation on a mark opens a note editor; notes keep their own stable text anchors when style spans split or merge.
- Browser-local autosave, with an honest fallback when storage is unavailable.
- Annotated HTML export embeds data and preserves the original page scripts. Each exported copy gets a separate notebook identity.
- A configurable starter with light/dark tokens, a small demo and pure-model/parser tests; no runtime dependencies.

I checked the current public PR and issue history. #58 concerns authored figure-part emphasis and #114 concerns model-synchronized explanations; neither covers reader-owned prose annotations or portable saved notes.

A draft implementation is prepared for scope feedback, following the request to open an issue before a feature PR. Would this optional learning-page layer fit the project?

## What this changes

Long-form standalone learning pages can optionally let a reader underline, color or highlight passages, attach editable plain-text notes, and export an offline HTML carrying those annotations. title: feat(kit): stage navigation — zoom/pan, readout bar, stage colours, auto-highlight, follow camera
body:
## What this changes

Adds `kit/stage-nav.mjs`, an opt-in navigation layer for framework-free pages, and makes it the default for new figures in `SKILL.md`:

- Wheel zoom around the cursor (up to 8×), drag pan with a 4px threshold so clicks on parts still work, and reset (double-click, `0`, button).
- The readout becomes a large explanation bar across the bottom of the card (22px, 16px on phones), tinted with the active stage's colour.
- For figures with two or more stages: a colour token per stage (`--anatomy-stage-1…8`, dark values with light overrides), legend chips with hover focus, **auto-highlight** of the running step (`H`) and a **follow camera** that eases in on it (`F`). Wheel or drag hands control back to the reader.

Wiring is one wrapper per assembly (`zoneGroup(zone, asm, svg)`) and a `shot()` callback that names the assemblies of the step running now. `references/stage-nav.md` documents the contract and rules, `references/kit.md` lists the API, and `scripts/stage-nav.test.mjs` covers the build helpers.

## Why

On a six-stage process figure (a Hero), a reader reported, in order: the machine was too small to read; the drawing is grey, so hover focus barely showed; the 10.5px corner readout was missed entirely; during the tour it was unclear which stage was running; and the camera alone was not enough without a highlight. Each item above is the fix that was tested on that figure. Making it the default means new figures ship with it instead of the reader having to ask.

Happy to move this to an issue first or split it (zoom/pan + readout bar vs. stage colours/highlight/camera) if you'd prefer. `SKILL.md`'s colour rule gains one exception: colour may tell the stages of a process apart.

title: iso-kit: keep roundedPlan from repeating a vertex when the radius fills a side
body:
## What this changes

`roundedPlan` (and so `slabOf`, `planOutline`, `ringOf`, `sideSeam`) no longer emits the same vertex twice when the corner radius fills a side. Fixed in `kit/iso-kit.mjs` and its `kit/iso-kit.ts` twin, with a regression test (`scripts/rounded-plan-full-radius.test.mjs`) and a CHANGELOG line.

## Why

With `r` equal to half of `w` or `d` (a pill or circle), or larger so it is clamped to that, two corner arcs meet at one point. The zero-length edge between them counts as facing away from the viewer, so `extrude` split the outline, crease and side shading into extra pieces. `slabOf({w:10, d:10, r:5})` gave 12 outline pieces; `r: 4.9999` gave 4. Both tests fail before the change and pass after.

Pages that embed the kit changed by the kit text. In the arcade cabinet and desk computer the SVG also loses a few zero-length and doubled segments (for example `M140.8 363.4L140.8 363.4`). Dial indicator and ripple tank change only in the inlined kit.

title: Canvas editor — the "Fine, I'll just do it myself!" rearrangement helper
body:
### What are you asking for?

Something else

### The idea

This one is a bit meta. We've been exploring this awesome skill for a while now, but, as it sometimes happens, there are slight discrepancies between what the agent sees (be it through vision, VLM retelling, or reading code) and what human eyes see. And after some Nth round of "please just move the bar 3px to the left! not to the isometric left, the **absolute** left!", it was decided that we needed something like this.

So there you go, the self-help route for micro-edits that would take too long to explain where you could just drag the objects around the scene with your mouse.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e06868d-29c1-432b-a92b-1dd35abd45d1

• `scene.mjs` — the graph: node: [parent, dx, dy, dz], world position = the sum along the chain. One rule, one function, shared by page and build.
• `editor.mjs` — the injected runtime: drag, arrow nudge, z-order pad, RESET ALL, DOWNLOAD.
• `build.editor.mjs` — the build, which ends by baking the deltas into the page — and still runs auditOrExit, so the kit's own geometry audit gates every arranged result.
• `archiverse.html` — a self-contained example, agent-built and human-curated `anatomy skill` implementation: our archive machine, a press that moulds perishable input into sealed volumes. Open it, press E, drag freely with mouse, or make isometric-friendly nudges with keyboard arrows.

[archiverse.html](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33614180/archiverse.html)

### Kind of figure

None

### Why it is worth adding

Placement is the one stage of figure-making that is a judgement call made with eyes. The skill's core workflow covers inventing, building, and verifying — but not hand-curating position after the fact (there's no cure for perfectionism). Thirteen prompt iterations got our figure 95% right, and every fix moved something else; one evening of dragging finished it.

The transferable parts:
1. **Scene graph as SSOT.** `total(node) = delta(node) + total(parent(node))` — the same function in the runtime and the build, so the page cannot disagree with its own file.
2. **Deltas-only files.** Our v1 mixed base offsets with deltas, indistinguishably — it cost us a "rubber-band on reload" bug (plan units applied as screen units, shrunk 1.8× and mirrored). v2 says what it means.
3. **Z-order belongs to the file.** Paint order is a curation decision; it rides in the JSON and applies the moment the page opens.

Honest limits: layout only (moves existing nodes, never creates parts); no live audit while dragging (the audit gates the build, not the drag); tested on one figure.

### What you tried instead

Verbal interventions, screenshots, messy hand-edits, at least *some* crying. Prompt-nudging resolved in each fix regressing something else; and at times, what makes sense math-wise looks plain odd to the human eye. In the end, it's coordinates-as-data is what survived.

[Gist to poke around](https://gist.github.com/Glassscale/cbeff489903b262ff661450a1c670d46). MIT, attribution not required but will be celebrated giddily — if any part is worth adapting, do take it. For all the folks out there aching to make just a couple of tiny adjustments, or perhaps play around freely with a building block set their agent prepared — know that you are seen.

### Before you submit

- [x] I searched the existing issues.
- [x] I read the Limits section of the README.

title: drive.mjs: validate shot and turn arguments before starting Chrome
body:
## Problem
`drive.mjs` validates `orbit` and `sheet` arguments before it starts Chrome (#67), but `shot` and `turn` go straight through:
- `["turn", "x"]` and `["turn"]` build `window.__isoTurn.set(NaN)` from `Number(value)` and the run carries on as if the figure had turned.
- A non-numeric `turn` group name, or a `shot` with a missing or non-string file name, a zero or non-numeric scale, or a region that is not four numbers, only fails once Chrome is running (a CDP "Invalid parameters" error, or a TypeError after the screenshot was already taken).

## Evidence
On current `main`, with a stand-in `CHROME_PATH` (so nothing real launches), every one of these actions gets as far as starting the browser, e.g. `[["turn","x"]]`, `[["shot"]]`, `[["shot","a.png",null,0]]` all fail with `Chrome exited before startup`, not with an argument error. The new test asserts exit 1 and a specific message for 11 bad forms; it fails on `main` and passes with this change.

## Change
`shot` and `turn` are checked in the existing pre-launch loop: `shot` needs a file name, an optional selector string, an optional scale above 0 and an optional `[x, y, w, h]` region with positive size; `turn` needs a finite angle (or an object of finite angles when no group is given) and an optional group name string. Documented forms (including `null` placeholders and the object form of `turn`) still pass; a second test covers those. CHANGELOG updated.

## Verified
- `node --test scripts/drive-shot-turn-values.test.mjs`: both tests pass (fail before the change).

## Not verified
- No real Chrome: I did not run the browser-driven drive tests in this environment, so the full suite was not run. The change is pure argument validation that runs before Chrome starts.
- Touches the same pre-launch loop as #94; whichever merges second may need a trivial rebase.

title: Example figure: espresso machine (heat exchanger, E61 group, 9 bar / 93 °C)
body:
### What are you asking for?

A new example figure

### The idea

An espresso machine with its side panel off: a single-boiler heat-exchanger machine with an E61 group, the kind found in most home and small café setups. The figure explains why espresso needs about 9 bar and about 93 °C, and how one boiler can make steam and brew water at the same time.

What moves, in order, when you press brew:

1. Water is drawn from the reservoir by a vibratory pump (up to about 15 bar).
2. The over-pressure valve bleeds the excess back to the tank, so the group sees about 9 bar.
3. The cold water runs through the heat-exchanger tube inside the steam boiler (about 1.2 bar, about 122 °C) and comes out at brewing temperature, about 93 °C.
4. In the E61 group the water first pre-infuses the puck at low pressure for a few seconds, then full pressure builds.
5. 18 g of coffee in a 58 mm portafilter gives about 36 g of espresso in 25 to 30 s.

Between shots, the thermosiphon loop between the boiler and the group keeps circulating hot water, which is what keeps the heavy brass group at temperature.

A readout driven by one model: brew pressure (bar), group water temperature (°C), shot time (s) and grams in the cup, the same numbers a barista reads off the gauge and the scale. Opening the steam valve drops the boiler pressure on the second gauge, and the heating element switches back on to recover it.

WebGL layers: the espresso stream with crema, and the steam from the wand.

### Kind of figure

SVG + WebGL

### Why it is worth adding

It is an everyday machine with a lot of hidden engineering: a pump, a pressure valve, a heat exchanger, a thermosiphon loop and two pressure regimes in one boiler. Most people use one every day without knowing how it works. It sits between the ripple tank (fluids) and the Raptor (pressure, heat and pipework), but as a kitchen object at a friendly scale, and every number in it can be checked on a real machine.

I work on software for connected coffee machines, so I know this mechanism well. I would like to build it myself and open a pull request that follows CONTRIBUTING: both themes, the geometry audit, line ends and 4× close-ups of every joint.

### What you tried instead

Nothing yet. I am opening this first, as CONTRIBUTING asks for larger changes, to agree on the approach before building it.

### Before you submit

- [x] I searched the existing issues.
- [x] I read the Limits section of the README.

title: Bug: `A.settle` does not order a tube thinner than three grid cells, so a wire can be drawn over the plate it hides behind
body:
### Where is the problem?

The kit (kit/)

### Which agent?

Other

### Kind of figure

SVG

### Where does the figure live?

Standalone HTML

### Theme

Both

### What happened

`overlapsOf` (and so `A.settle`) finds no overlap between a recorded tube and a solid when the tube is thinner than about two grid cells on screen. At the default `step` of 0.25 that is a tube under 0.5 px wide. At 0.5 px it is found in most directions but not all; from 0.625 px up it was found in every case I tried. The pair gets no order rule and the item keeps the key it was given from its centre point. When that key is wrong, the tube is drawn over a plate it passes behind, and `--audit` still prints `audit passed`, because `depthOrder` only checks pairs that `overlapsOf` found.

I met it in a figure of four upright plates standing on a bench, with 78 straight wires (radius 0.1, scale 1.07, so 0.21 px wide) between them. Each wire starts on a hidden pin behind its sending plate and ends on a unit of the next plate. With the default step:

- `A.settle` finds 45 overlaps; with the fix in the pull request that follows this issue it finds 406.
- Two wires (the first of the top row, which rises to the next plate) kept a key after their own plate. Their first pixels show over the plate.
- `node scripts/lines.mjs` reports `line ends: 1 of 1066 ends on 187 lines float` (a wire start 1.24 px from anything), in both themes. The audit has no failing line.

The pin is not part of it. It is a recorded solid and not an item, so `settle` never looks at it. A tube with the same radius, started behind a plate with nothing else in the figure, shows the same thing (script below).

## Why

`overlapsOf` ray-casts both shapes on a grid of `step`, flags the cells where one surface is more than `tolerance` nearer, then closes the flagged cells (one dilate, one erode) and erodes once more "so the hairline along a real contact drops out". A tube whose screen width is about a cell or less leaves a one-cell-wide trail. The close does not widen it and the erosion removes all of it, so the side's area is 0, below `least`, and `measure` returns `null`.

For the repro below, at `step: 0.25`, radius 0.1, scale 1.2: 203 cells are flagged for the plate and the area is 0. At `step: 0.1`: 1270 cells, area 7.49 px², one pair.

How wide a tube has to be, measured on the unfixed kit: the same plate and a tube behind it, 13 directions across the screen times 5 offsets (65 cases), scale 1.2, step 0.25:

| tube width in cells | found |
|---|---|
| 1 | 10 / 65 |
| 1.5 | 13 / 65 |
| 2 | 56 / 65 |
| 2.5 | 65 / 65 |
| 3 | 65 / 65 |

(Scale 1.073 gives 10, 14, 54, 65, 65.) That agrees with the note in `references/kit.md` that a cable under three cells wide read as noise at step 0.5.

Passing `step: 0.1` to `A.settle` finds the pair, but it took about 6× the time on this figure and a thinner wire needs a smaller step again; the cost grows with the square of it.

### What you expected

A tube that passes behind a plate is ordered behind it however thin it is, as a thicker one is. Failing that, the audit should say that a shape was too thin to be ordered.

### How to reproduce

Save as `repro.mjs` in the repository root and run `node repro.mjs`. It is a plate 56 wide, 8 deep and 156 tall that stands along y, and a wire that starts 2.5 behind it and rises away from the viewer. The wire's key from its midpoint is above the plate's, which is wrong, and `settle` has to correct it.

```js
import * as A from "./kit/audit.mjs";

const P = { origin: [0, 0], scale: 1.2, azimuth: 40, elevation: 30 };
const plate = { x: -28, y: -4, w: 56, d: 8, r: 1.5 };
const from = [0, -6.5, 125];
const to = [0, -100, 181];

for (const radius of [0.1, 0.2]) {
  const R = A.recorder(P);
  R.put({ name: "plate", at: [0, 0, 83], shapes: [A.slab(plate, 5, 156, { name: "plate" }, 4)] });
  R.put({ name: "wire", at: [0, -53.25, 153], shapes: [A.tube([from, to], radius, { name: "wire" })] });
  const { overlaps } = A.settle(R, P);
  const [a, b] = R.items;
  console.log(`radius ${radius}: ${overlaps.pairs.length} overlaps, plate key ${a.key.toFixed(2)}, wire key ${b.key.toFixed(2)}, ${b.key > a.key ? "wire is drawn over the plate" : "plate is drawn over the wire"}`);
}
```

### Output

On `main` (1482e84):

```
radius 0.1: 0 overlaps, plate key 41.50, wire key 46.86, wire is drawn over the plate
radius 0.2: 1 overlaps, plate key 46.88, wire key 46.86, plate is drawn over the wire
```

### Environment

Node.js v26.12.0, macOS 27.0, Google Chrome 155.0.8059.80 (only for `scripts/lines.mjs`; the script above needs no browser).

### Screenshots

None. The visible fault is the first pixel or so of one 0.35 px wire over a plate face; `scripts/lines.mjs` reports it better than a close-up does.

title: `A.settle`: order a tube thinner than three grid cells
body:
## What this changes

`overlapsOf` (and so `A.settle`) now ray-casts a tube whose screen width is under three cells (`2 · radius · scale < 3 · step`, 0.75 px at the default step) as a tube three cells wide. Its points move back along the view by `reach − radius` at each end, so its nearest surface stays at its true depth. Tubes of three cells or more, and every other shape, are measured as before.

The change is in `rasterOf` in `kit/audit.mjs` (8 lines). `references/kit.md` gets one sentence under `overlapsOf` and `CHANGELOG.md` one line under Fixed.

`scripts/audit-thin-tube.test.mjs` has three tests, a plate and a tube 0.05 in radius on a diagonal, camera straight on:

- the tube behind the plate gets a key before the plate's;
- the tube in front of the plate gets a key after the plate's;
- a tube whose nearest surface is 0.5 behind the plate's front face is still ordered behind it. Widening without the shift back put it 0.325 nearer, inside `tolerance`, and the pair vanished again.

## Why

A tube about a cell wide leaves a one-cell trail in the flagged cells. The close and erode in `regionOf` do not widen it, the erosion removes it, its area is 0 and `measure` returns `null`. The item then keeps the key it got from its centre point. If that key is wrong, the tube is drawn over a plate it passes behind, and `--audit` prints `audit passed`, because `depthOrder` only checks the pairs that `overlapsOf` found. Details and numbers are in the issue (#128).

I hit it in a figure with four upright plates and 78 straight wires of radius 0.1 (0.21 px at scale 1.07), each starting on a hidden pin behind its sending plate. I removed the figure's workaround (clamping two wires' keys below the plate's after `settle`) and built it against `main` and against this change:

| | `main` | this change |
|---|---|---|
| overlaps found by `A.settle` | 45 | 406 |
| wires keyed after their sending plate | 2 (`w0.0-0`, `w1.0-0`) | 0 |
| `lines.mjs`, dark | `1 of 1066`, start 1.24 px from anything | `0 of 1066` |
| `lines.mjs`, light | `1 of 1066`, start 1.24 px from anything | `0 of 1066` |
| `--audit` | `audit passed` | `audit passed`, 0 problems on every line |

Process CPU time up to the end of `settle` is 2.3 s on both. A smaller `step` finds the pair too (`step: 0.1`, 267 overlaps, 0 late wires) but costs about 6 times as much (wall time), and a thinner wire needs a smaller step again. Widening the tube costs nothing extra, because the grid does not change.

Why three cells: on `main`, a plate with a tube behind it, 13 directions times 5 offsets, step 0.25, scale 1.2, found 10/65 at 1 cell wide, 13/65 at 1.5, 56/65 at 2, 65/65 at 2.5 and 65/65 at 3. Three leaves some margin.

Every example is unchanged. Only three examples call `A.settle` (arcade-cabinet, turning-dial with its stress build, raptor-engine). I counted the tubes this change widens while building all of them in both themes (and `turning-dial --light --verify`, `stress.mjs --light`): none. `git status --short` after the builds shows only the files of this change. The Raptor `--audit` run was not repeated, because the pages it checks are byte-identical.

Not covered: a thin solid (a 0.2 wide box or a thin rod) may have the same problem. I have not tried it, and a flush slab 0.6 thick would need a different test, since its footprint is not thin when seen face on.

## Checks

- [x] Every example rebuilds, and `git status --short` shows only the changes I meant. arcade-cabinet, turning-dial (and `--verify`, `stress.mjs`) and raptor-engine, dark and light. The other examples do not use `kit/audit.mjs`.
- [x] No comments in code.
- [x] Kit changes are opt-in, and every existing example is byte-identical. The new path is taken only by a tube under three cells wide, and no example has one.
- [x] I built and looked at both themes. The figure above in both, and the examples in both.
- [x] Figures with pipes, cables or round parts: `node build.mjs --audit` ends `audit passed`. Run on arcade-cabinet (1290 overlaps, 0 problems) and on the figure above. Not repeated on raptor-engine or turning-dial, whose pages come out byte-identical.
- [x] `node scripts/lines.mjs` prints `line ends: 0` on both themes and in every resting pose. On the figure above at rest, dark and light. The examples' pages are unchanged.
- [ ] Shaders. No shader change.
- [ ] 3D. `turning-dial` pages are byte-identical; I did not run the full orbit audit.
- [x] Every number in the figure, the readout, the caption and the docs is true.
- [x] A line under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`.

`node --test scripts/audit-*.test.mjs scripts/turn-*.test.mjs`: 107 pass, 0 fail (three of those files drive Chrome and need `CHROME_PATH` on my machine). The rest of `scripts/*.test.mjs` needs the React install from CI and I did not run it. Without the change to `rasterOf` the three new tests fail, and without the shift back the third one fails.

## Screenshots

None. The fault on the page is the first pixel of one 0.35 px wire over a plate, and `lines.mjs` reports it better than a close-up. Nothing is drawn differently in any example.


Fixes #128.

title: `lines.mjs`: do not judge line ends outside a clipping svg
body:
## What this changes

`scripts/line-ends.mjs` skips a line end when the line's svg clips (its `overflow` is not `visible`) and the end lies outside the svg's box. That end is not checked and not counted in `line ends: N of M`. A line with one end off-stage is still judged on the end that is on-stage. Ends inside the box, and every end in an svg with `overflow: visible` (the kit's `.iso-svg`), are judged exactly as before.

`scripts/lines.test.mjs` gets three tests:

- an off-stage end next to a rooted on-stage end passes (`0 of 1`);
- an off-stage end next to a floating on-stage end still fails (`1 of 1`);
- the same line in an svg with `overflow: visible` still fails (`2 of 2`).

The test helper takes an optional `viewBox`, `style` and `shape`; the two existing tests call it as before. `lines.mjs --help`, `references/verify.md` ("Line ends") and `CHANGELOG.md` mention it.

## Why

A page that zooms by easing the svg's `viewBox` (click a part, the figure flies to it) keeps the whole figure in the DOM. Wires, ribs and seams that start off-stage are checked against the whole page, find nothing to land on, and are reported as floating although none of them is drawn.

Repro, a figure with four upright layer plates and straight weight lines, `.iso-stage` and `.iso-svg` set to `overflow: hidden`, `viewBox` eased from `0 0 780 500` to `252.7 100.1 300.1 192.4` by a click on a unit:

```sh
node scripts/drive.mjs nn.html '[["wait",800],["lines"],["click",".nn-unit[data-l=\"2\"][data-j=\"3\"]"],["wait",2500],["lines"],["key","Escape"],["wait",2500],["lines"]]'
```

| | at rest | zoomed | after Escape |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | `0 of 1066` | `5 of 1066`, each start 1.2 to 1.3 px from anything | `0 of 1066` |
| after | `0 of 1066` | `0 of 580` | `0 of 1066` |

All five are starts of wires that run behind their sending plate, outside the stage. Other zoom targets on the same page gave up to 13.

To check that a real fault is still caught while zoomed, I appended 24 short `iso-line` paths inside the zoomed box and one at `M20 20` outside it, with `--reduced` so the zoom is exact. `main` reports 35 ends and this change 28. The 7 that went are the two ends of the outside path and the five wire starts; the other 28 are the same ends on both.

At rest nothing changes. All 16 example pages, dark and light, print the same `lines.mjs` result before and after with `--reduced`, including the 16 ends already reported on `turning-stress-light.html`. Without `--reduced` the turning-dial pages vary from run to run on `main` too (`794 ends on 82 lines` and `792 ends on 74 lines` on two runs of the same build), so compare them with `--reduced`.

Not covered: an svg with `overflow: visible` inside a clipping container (a card with `overflow: hidden`) is still judged on its whole drawing. I kept the change to the svg's own box; the same test on the nearest clipping ancestor would cover it.

## Checks

- [ ] Every example rebuilds, and `git status --short` shows only the changes I meant. I did not rebuild: no example, kit or build script is touched.
- [x] No comments in code.
- [x] Kit changes are opt-in, and every existing example is byte-identical. No kit change.
- [ ] I built and looked at both themes. There is no visual change; both themes of every example went through `lines.mjs`.
- [ ] Figures with pipes, cables or round parts: `node build.mjs --audit`. No figure or kit change.
- [x] `node scripts/lines.mjs` prints `line ends: 0` on both themes and in every resting pose. The output is the same as before the change on every example.
- [ ] Shaders. No shader change.
- [ ] 3D. `turn-check.mjs --lines` runs the same function and the turning-dial pages print the same result with `--reduced`; I did not run the full orbit.
- [x] Every number in the figure, the readout, the caption and the docs is true.
- [x] A line under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`.

`node --test scripts/lines.test.mjs`: 5 pass; without the change to `line-ends.mjs` the first two new tests fail.

## Screenshots

None. The check prints text and nothing is drawn differently.

title: `lines.mjs`: follow `<use>` elements
body:
## What this changes

`scripts/line-ends.mjs` replaces each `<use>` that points at a `<g>` or a shape with a copy of its target (wrapped in a `<g>` that carries the use's attributes and `transform` plus `translate(x y)`) while it measures, then puts the original `<use>` back. Nested uses are followed up to 8 levels. A `<use>` of a `<symbol>`, an unknown id or an external file is left as it was.

Two things follow:

- a line that ends on an outline, dot or fill that comes from a `<use>` is judged against it;
- an `.iso-line` inside used content is checked like any other.

Pages without `<use>` take the same path as before.

`scripts/lines-use.test.mjs` has five tests: an end on a used outline is rooted; an end beside a used outline still floats; a used outline follows the `transform` on its use; a floating line inside used content is reported; the `<use>` elements are still in the page after the check. `CHANGELOG.md` has the line.

## Why

`line-ends.mjs` collects its shapes with `svg.querySelectorAll("path, line, ...")`. The content a `<use>` draws lives in a shadow tree, so that query never returns it, and the originals sit in `<defs>`, which the check skips. A figure that draws repeated parts with `<use>` therefore has outlines on screen that the check cannot see.

Repro: ten lipids in a 5×2 grid, each two `sphereOf` heads (20 heads) and two vertical `iso-line` tails that start and end on the heads' outline circles (40 ends). Same drawing three ways, `node scripts/lines.mjs page.html`:

| heads drawn as | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| inline `solidSvg(sphereOf(c, r, P))` | `0 of 40` | `0 of 40` |
| `<use href="#head" x y>` of one head at the origin | `40 of 40` | `0 of 40` |
| `<g transform="translate(x y)">` around a copy of the head | `0 of 40` | `0 of 40` |

On the `<use>` page the check sees 10 paths (the tails) and no outline; the inline page gives it 150 paths and 20 outlines. The `<g translate>` row applies the same unrounded translation without a `<use>` and passes, so rounding of the offsets is not the cause.

The same swap on a bilayer figure (68 lipids with 136 heads, 275 ends) gives `0` inline, `64` with `<use>` (33 starts, 31 ends), `0` with `<g translate>`, and `0` with `<use>` after this change. With `<use>`, an end only passes when it happens to land on another lipid's tail, which is why a grid reports only its outer edge.

All 11 example pages I ran (dial-indicator, push-button, desk-computer, arcade-cabinet in both themes; ripple-tank; raptor-engine light; turning-dial dark) print the same result before and after. No example contains a `<use>`.

Not covered: `<use>` of a `<symbol>` (its `viewBox` and `width`/`height` would need a viewport transform), and CSS that matches on the `<defs>` ancestry of the original.

## Checks

- [ ] Every example rebuilds, and `git status --short` shows only the changes I meant. I did not rebuild: no example, kit or build script is touched.
- [x] No comments in code.
- [x] Kit changes are opt-in, and every existing example is byte-identical. No kit change.
- [ ] I built and looked at both themes. There is no visual change; the check output is identical on the examples listed above.
- [ ] Figures with pipes, cables or round parts: `node build.mjs --audit`. No figure or kit change.
- [x] `node scripts/lines.mjs` prints `line ends: 0` on both themes and in every resting pose. Same output as before on every example I ran.
- [ ] Shaders. No shader change.
- [ ] 3D. `turn-check.mjs --lines` runs the same function; I ran it on `turning-dial.html` through `lines.mjs` only.
- [x] Every number in the figure, the readout, the caption and the docs is true.
- [x] A line under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`.

`node --test scripts/lines*.test.mjs scripts/curve-density.test.mjs scripts/capture-selector.test.mjs scripts/drive-actions.test.mjs`: 58 pass. Without the change to `line-ends.mjs`, three of the five new tests fail: the rooted end, the `transform` test and the floating line inside used content. The other two pass on `main` and guard the other side.

## Screenshots

Ring check on the `<use>` page, before (40 ends ringed) and after (none):

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/issue-figures/u3/u3-use-head.png)
![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/issue-figures/u3/u3-use-fixed.png)

title: Let pageHtml take extra CSS and plateHtml a slot under the figure
body:
## What this changes

`pageHtml` takes an optional `css` string, added to the page's `<style>` after the kit's rules. `plateHtml` takes an optional `below` string, placed inside the card right after `body`. Both default to empty, so a call that doesn't pass them returns the same HTML as before.

The kit reference documents both, there is a line under `Unreleased`, and `scripts/page-slots.test.mjs` covers the default and the option output.

Because `kitScript()` inlines `iso-kit.mjs`, the pages that call it carry the new default parameters in their inlined copy. The 10 affected pages are rebuilt and included; each changes by the same 4 lines and nothing else. The raptor-engine and turning-dial pages are byte-identical.

## Why

A figure that has a text bar under it, or that zooms its `viewBox`, has no way to say so through the page builders today. It puts a `<style>` inside `body`, and either appends the bar to `body` or splices it into the finished card with `String.replace`. A page that zooms also has to switch `.iso-svg` from `overflow:visible` to `hidden`, so the zoomed picture doesn't spill out of the card; that rule has to travel the same way.

I hit this in four figures (an attention map, a neural network, a neuron and a cell zoom). Each ended up with the same string workaround. With these two options the same figures build without touching the card markup, and the attention figure renders pixel for pixel the same as before.

I left `overflow` as a plain CSS rule through `css` rather than a dedicated option, since it is one declaration and `kit.md` now shows it.

## Checks

- [x] Every example rebuilds, and `git status --short` shows only the 10 pages that inline the kit, each changed by the same 4 lines.
- [x] No comments in code.
- [x] Kit changes are opt-in, and every existing example's output is the same; the 10 pages that inline the kit differ only in that inlined copy, and are committed here.
- [x] Both themes: no figure changes, so nothing new to look at; the pages differ only in script text.
- [ ] Audit: not applicable, no geometry changed.
- [ ] `scripts/lines.mjs`: not applicable, no markup changed.
- [ ] Shaders, 3D: not applicable.
- [x] `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs`: 294 pass.
- [x] Every number and claim in the docs is one I checked.
- [x] A line under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`.

title: Bug: `lines.mjs` judges a tick against 7 viewBox px, so the same tick passes or fails when the figure is refit
body:
### Where is the problem?

A check script (scripts/)

### Which agent?

Other

### Kind of figure

Not about a figure

### Where does the figure live?

Not about a figure

### Theme

Not about a figure

### What happened

`line-ends.mjs` treats a straight line of at most `mark = 7` as a tick: one end may float if the other is rooted within 2 px. A longer straight line has to be rooted at both ends within 1 px. The lengths are compared in viewBox px (`length <= mark * scale`, with `scale` the svg's screen scale), so they are the projected lengths. A world length L becomes L × `P.scale` × the tick's foreshortening, and `P.scale` is whatever `fitProjection` came out with. The same ruler, with the same world geometry, passes at one canvas size and fails at another.

I met this building an attention-map figure: its major ruler ticks were 7 world units, 11.6 px at its fit (`P.scale` ≈ 1.66), and `lines.mjs` reported four floating ends. Making the ticks 4 units long fixed it. The rule is fine as such; what is missing is any hint that the same tick is judged differently in a bigger or smaller figure.

Two repros, both on the kit as it is.

**1. A ruler strip with 5-unit major ticks, only the `fitProjection` canvas changes** ([`ruler-build.mjs`](https://github.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/blob/issue-figures/u4/ruler-build.mjs), same world strip and ticks every time):

| canvas | `P.scale` | major tick | `lines.mjs` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 300 × 190 | 0.673 | 3.37 px | `line ends: 0 of 112` |
| 450 × 285 | 1.118 | 5.59 px | `line ends: 0 of 112` |
| 600 × 380 | 1.548 | 7.74 px | `line ends: 14 of 112` |
| 900 × 570 | 2.408 | 12.04 px | `line ends: 22 of 112` |

**2. `examples/dial-indicator/build.mjs` with only `WIDTH` and `HEIGHT` changed** (the height keeps the 600:380 shape; every world dimension, the ticks included, is untouched):

| canvas | `P.scale` | major ruler tick (3.6 units) | `lines.mjs` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 600 × 380 (as shipped) | 1.101 | 4.09 px | `line ends: 0 of 367` |
| 720 × 456 | 1.363 | 5.06 px | `line ends: 0 of 367` |
| 840 × 532 | 1.624 | 6.03 px | `line ends: 0 of 367` |
| 960 × 608 | 1.886 | 7.00 px | `line ends: 14 of 367` (the seven major ticks, both ends each) |
| 1200 × 760 | 2.409 | 8.94 px | `line ends: 65 of 367` |

Ringed output at 960, then the 600 page for comparison:

![960](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/issue-figures/u4/dial-960-ringed-original-checker.png)
![600](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/issue-figures/u4/dial-600-ringed-original-checker.png)

The viewport is not the cause. The 600 × 380 dial prints `0 of 367` at `--width 390` and `--width 1440`, and the 5-unit ruler at 600 × 380 prints `14 of 112` at `--width 390`, `800` and `1440` (the svg is 334 and 852 CSS px wide at 390 and 1440).

To reproduce the first table from a clone (`shots/` is ignored):

```sh
mkdir -p shots
curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/issue-figures/u4/ruler-build.mjs -o shots/ruler-build.mjs
node shots/ruler-build.mjs --width 450 --height 285 --major 5 --out shots/ruler-450.html
node shots/ruler-build.mjs --width 600 --height 380 --major 5 --out shots/ruler-600.html
node scripts/lines.mjs shots/ruler-450.html
node scripts/lines.mjs shots/ruler-600.html
```

### What you expected

The same tick, the same world length on the same strip, gets the same verdict whatever canvas the figure is fitted to. Failing that, `references/verify.md` ("up to 7 px") and `lines.mjs --help` say that the limit is in viewBox px at this figure's fit.

### How to reproduce

See the two tables and the commands above.

### Possible fixes

1. Document only: say "7 viewBox px" in `references/verify.md` and the `--help` text, and tell authors that changing the canvas can move ticks across it.
2. Let the caller set it: `lines.mjs` forwards only `{ tolerance }` to the check, though `lineEnds` already takes `mark`. Today it is reachable with `drive.mjs … '[["lines", null, null, { "mark": 9 }]]'`. A `--mark` flag would make it one line, but the author still has to convert a world length to px by hand for every fit.
3. Judge ticks in world units. The figure states its projection scale (`data-scale="<P.scale>"` on the svg, for example from `figureSvg({ …, scale: P.scale })`) and the check compares the length with `markWorld * scale`. An svg without the attribute keeps the 7 viewBox px rule, so nothing changes for existing figures until they opt in.

I tried 3 in the check only ([`u4-poc.patch`](https://github.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/blob/issue-figures/u4/u4-poc.patch): `markWorld = 4.5` and `markLimit = Number(owner.getAttribute("data-scale")) * markWorld || mark`). With the attribute added to the ruler pages (`ruler-build.mjs --stamp`), 3.6-unit ticks pass at 300, 450, 600 and 900, and 5-unit ticks fail at all four (10, 11, 14 and 22 ends), where without the attribute they pass at the two small canvases. `scripts/lines-mark-scale.test.mjs` has four cases: 6 px and 12 px without the attribute behave as before, and the same 12 px tick passes at `data-scale="3"` (4 units) and fails at `data-scale="1.5"` (8 units). On the original `line-ends.mjs` the third case fails, on the patched one all four pass, and the five other `lines*.test.mjs` files (23 tests) still pass. `examples/dial-indicator` still prints `0 of 367` on both themes.

Open points before this can be a pull request:

- The default. I used 4.5 units only to separate my two test lengths. 7 px is 6.4 units at the dial's shipped scale (1.10) and 4.5 units at the ruler's (1.55), so no single value reproduces today's verdict everywhere. The major ticks in the examples run from 2.4 to 5.2 world units (5.2 is the ripple-tank's side ruler), and a default below the longest of them could make an example that opts in start failing. I have not measured each example's ticks in px, so that needs doing before a default is chosen.
- Who writes `data-scale`. `figureSvg` in `kit/iso-kit.ts` and `.mjs` is the obvious place, and `IsoFigure` in `kit/react/draw.tsx`. Existing examples would only pick it up when `build.mjs` passes it, which changes their built pages by one attribute.
- Direction still counts. This removes the dependence on the fit, not on the direction of the tick: at azimuth 20° and the ruler's fit, a 5-unit tick is 5.8 px along x and 9.6 px along y (at the default 45° they are equal), so one world length is not one px length inside a figure either.
- `tolerance` (1) and the root slack (2) are viewBox px as well. That is why the 5-unit ticks above count 10, 11, 14, 22 floating ends rather than the same number: at the smallest canvas some of them end within 1 px of the strip's far edge.

I can open the pull request for 3 once you have picked the unit and the default, or for 1 or 2 alone if you prefer that.

title: Proposal: per-part surface tone and an opaque dim state for selection
body:
### What are you asking for? A new part or helper in the kit ### The idea Two small, opt-in additions, so a figure can say how heavy one part is and which parts should recede, without hand-writing a token set per theme: - `data-surface="mid"` or `"hi"`: the part's fills (face, top, the four shades, tube bodies) are mixed toward `--anatomy-hi`. That is lighter in dark and darker in light, so it is the fill counterpart of the line tones `mid` and `hi`. - `data-dim`: the part's fills are mixed toward the card, its line tones drop (`hi` to `lo`, `mid` and `lo` to `faint`, `lit` to `mid`, dots to `mid`), and it stays fully opaque, so it still hides whatever is behind it. Both only override tokens that the existing rules already read, so they work on a solid's root `` or on a wrapper group, and `data-lit`, the `data-seamless` strokes and face text follow without any new selector. The `.tb-*` tube fills read the same tokens, so a tube group should follow too. A selected part would be `data-lit` plus `data-surface="hi"`, with `data-dim` on everything else. If this is the right shape, `solidSvg` and the React `Solid` take `surface` and `dim` and emit the attributes. Unset, they emit nothing, the way `lit` does today, so existing pages do not change. #### Prototype CSS only (21 lines), and no other file changes. I appended it to a built `dial-indicator` page and set the attributes from a page script: `data-surface="hi"` and `data-lit` on the carriage and plunger, `data-dim` on every other top-level item.
kit/iso-tone.css (also here) ```css .iso{ --anatomy-base-paper:var(--anatomy-paper);--anatomy-base-face:var(--anatomy-face);--anatomy-base-top:var(--anatomy-top); --anatomy-base-shade-0:var(--anatomy-shade-0);--anatomy-base-shade-1:var(--anatomy-shade-1);--anatomy-base-shade-2:var(--anatomy-shade-2);--anatomy-base-shade-3:var(--anatomy-shade-3); --anatomy-base-lit-top:var(--anatomy-lit-top);--anatomy-base-lit-shade:var(--anatomy-lit-shade); --anatomy-surface-mid:10%;--anatomy-surface-hi:24%;--anatomy-dim-mix:78%; --anatomy-dim-hi:var(--anatomy-lo);--anatomy-dim-mid:var(--anatomy-faint);--anatomy-dim-lo:var(--anatomy-faint);--anatomy-dim-lit:var(--anatomy-mid);--anatomy-dim-dot:var(--anatomy-mid); } [data-surface="mid"]{--tone-to:var(--anatomy-hi);--tone-k:var(--anatomy-surface-mid)} [data-surface="hi"]{--tone-to:var(--anatomy-hi);--tone-k:var(--anatomy-surface-hi)} [data-dim]{--tone-to:var(--anatomy-card);--tone-k:var(--anatomy-dim-mix);--anatomy-hi:var(--anatomy-dim-hi);--anatomy-mid:var(--anatomy-dim-mid);--anatomy-lo:var(--anatomy-dim-lo);--anatomy-lit:var(--anatomy-dim-lit);--anatomy-dot:var(--anatomy-dim-dot)} :is([data-surface],[data-dim]){ --anatomy-paper:color-mix(in srgb,var(--anatomy-base-paper),var(--tone-to) var(--tone-k)); --anatomy-face:color-mix(in srgb,var(--anatomy-base-face),var(--tone-to) var(--tone-k)); --anatomy-top:color-mix(in srgb,var(--anatomy-base-top),var(--tone-to) var(--tone-k)); --anatomy-shade-0:color-mix(in srgb,var(--anatomy-base-shade-0),var(--tone-to) var(--tone-k)); --anatomy-shade-1:color-mix(in srgb,var(--anatomy-base-shade-1),var(--tone-to) var(--tone-k)); --anatomy-shade-2:color-mix(in srgb,var(--anatomy-base-shade-2),var(--tone-to) var(--tone-k)); --anatomy-shade-3:color-mix(in srgb,var(--anatomy-base-shade-3),var(--tone-to) var(--tone-k)); --anatomy-lit-top:color-mix(in srgb,var(--anatomy-base-lit-top),var(--tone-to) var(--tone-k)); --anatomy-lit-shade:color-mix(in srgb,var(--anatomy-base-lit-shade),var(--tone-to) var(--tone-k)); } ```
The `--anatomy-base-*` and `--anatomy-dim-*` copies are defined once on `.iso`. A `var()` on an element sees that element's own overrides, so a part cannot define `--anatomy-shade-0` as a mix of `var(--anatomy-shade-0)` directly. Left to right: `data-lit` as it is today, `opacity: .3` on every other item, and the prototype. ![dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/issue-figures/u6/u6-states-dark.png) ![light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/issue-figures/u6/u6-states-light.png) At 5× around the magnet base (light theme): `opacity: .3` first, the prototype second. With opacity the plate's groove, screw ring and ruler ticks show through the base and the post shows through its top. With `data-dim` the base hides them. ![opacity, 5x](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/issue-figures/u6/u6-bleed-5x-light.png) ![data-dim, 5x](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/issue-figures/u6/u6-dim-5x-light.png) Contrast ratios (WCAG, from the computed fills in Chrome): | | dark | light | |---|---|---| | lit top vs plain top, today | 1.13 : 1 | 1.00 : 1 | | selected top vs dim top, prototype | 2.26 : 1 | 1.58 : 1 | | dim top vs card | 1.02 : 1 | 1.01 : 1 | | dim edge vs card (today's `lo` edge) | 1.29 : 1 (1.74) | 1.43 : 1 (2.00) | The percentages (24, 10, 78) are first guesses. A dim part's fill is almost the card colour, so its edges carry it; that is the intended ghost look, and it is still opaque. With the CSS appended and no attributes set, the `dial-indicator` page renders the same pixels in both themes (headless Chrome, reduced motion, PNG hashes equal). Not done: the `solidSvg` and `Solid` options, docs, a figure that uses it, and a tube group (`dial-indicator` has none). A `solidSvg` with `halo: true` keeps its shadow when dimmed. `data-dim` and `data-lit` on the same element are not defined. #### Questions 1. Where should the CSS live? `ISO_CSS` is inlined into every built page, so adding the tokens there changes the bytes of every committed example (no visual change). I would keep the byte-identical rule and ship an opt-in `ISO_TONE_CSS` (and `kit/iso-tone.css`) that `pageHtml` and `figureSvg` add when asked. The other way is to put it in `ISO_CSS` and rebuild all the example pages in the same PR. Which do you prefer? 2. Are `surface` and `dim` the right names? The steps `mid` and `hi` follow the line tones. 3. `surface="hi"` goes toward the ink, so in light it makes a part grayer and never whiter. Is that the right direction, or should light stay white and only `lo` sink? 4. Is `data-lit` plus `data-surface="hi"` enough, or do you want `data-lit` itself stronger in dark? That would change the existing examples. 5. For value-driven fills (a heat colouring of a grid by weight) would you want a continuous `--anatomy-surface-k` on top of the two steps? I did not prototype it. I am not asking for a PR yet. If the shape is agreed I would send the CSS, the two options and one doc paragraph each in `craft.md` and `motion.md`, with the rebuilt pages if you choose the other CSS home. ### Kind of figure SVG ### Why it is worth adding I built four figures against an unmodified copy of the kit to see where it stops outside the machine examples: a 10 by 10 attention grid, a neuron, a small neural net and a cell, mitochondrion, ATP synthase zoom. Three limits came up in all of them. **`data-lit` is one weak step in dark.** In dark every plain fill token sits between `#0f0f0f` and `#1c1c1c`, and `--anatomy-lit-top` is `#262626`. A lit top is 1.13 : 1 against a plain top. The four side shades are replaced by one `#1d1d1d` (`.iso-solid[data-lit]>.iso-shade` outranks `[data-shade]`; I read the computed fills: four values on a plain solid, one on a lit one), which is 1.05 : 1 against shade 3. So a lit part is told apart by its white edge, and an edge in `hi` (`#d4d4d4`) against `lit` (`#ffffff`) is 1.48 : 1 (1.39 : 1 in light, `#26262a` against `#000000`). In light `--anatomy-lit-top` is `#ffffff`, the same as `--anatomy-top`, so the top fill does not change at all. In the attention grid the bars could not use `hi` edges, because they could no longer be told from the lit row; they were limited to `mid` and `lo` and carried the weight by height alone. **There is no tone for a part's fill.** The tone hierarchy in `craft.md` (base `lo`, structure `mid`, subject `hi`) exists only for edges; all fills come from one ramp. Each figure that wants a darker plate and a lighter unit writes its own token set per theme: - The neural net sets `--anatomy-paper`, `--anatomy-shade-0` to `-3` and `--anatomy-top` on `.nn-layer` and again on `.nn-unit`, with a light copy: 24 values. - The neuron lifts the whole dark ramp to `#2c2c2c` to `#6c6c6c`, because the figure read as near-black with the kit's fills, and resets it for the floor tray. - In the examples, the test rig keeps `--ms-glass-top: #262626` and `--ms-glass-lit-top: #2e2e2e` (light: `#fefefd`, `#fffffe`) for its glass, and the desk computer maps `.pc-well`, `.pc-bezel` and `.pc-dark` to chosen ramp steps by hand. - The attention grid wanted a fill that follows the weight. There is no fill channel, so it was not possible. **Opacity is not a usable dim.** The parts are painted back to front with opaque fills, and `opacity` on an item shows whatever was painted behind it. The neuron saw the overlaps show through each other at `0.22` (about 300 interleaved groups), and the attention grid gave up dimming the unselected rows because the bars behind showed through. The workaround was a dim token set per group, 13 variables per theme in the neuron's CSS. The screenshots above show the same on `dial-indicator` at `0.3`. #### Machine figures have the same need - `raptor.css` has about 30 lines (`.rp-stage[data-focus] .it:not([data-on])` and `.it[data-on]`) that make the selected assembly `lit` and step the others down. It steps only line tones; fills are not dimmed. `references/motion.md` describes the same recipe in its Selection paragraph. - In that block, `--anatomy-hi: var(--anatomy-mid)` and `--anatomy-mid: var(--anatomy-lo)` sit on one element. Each `var()` sees the element's own override, so `hi` resolves to `lo` (checked in Chrome with the same two declarations), a drop of two tones where `motion.md` says one. This is easy to get wrong by hand. - `arcade-cabinet.css` repeats what `data-lit` does in three rules for the lamps, whose state sits on a wrapper group (`.ac-lamp[data-on]`) where `data-lit` has no effect, and adds three more that undo it for two of them. - Zoom levels (#51) and exploded views also want a state where one part stays and the rest recedes, and opacity would bleed there in the same way. ### What you tried instead Per-figure token overrides on a wrapper class (in my four figures, and in the Raptor and the test rig), `opacity` on interleaved groups (rejected, see above), and edge-only highlights, which leave fills unchanged and so give a lit part very little against its neighbours in dark. ### Before you submit - [X] I searched the existing issues. - [X] I read the Limits section of the README.

title: Proposal: partial revolution and cut faces for lathe (follow-up to #51)
body:
### What are you asking for?

A new part or helper in the kit

### The idea

`lathe` always turns a profile through a full 360°, and `sphereOf` is always a whole ball. A zoom (#51) that goes into a round part has to show that part opened: a wedge out of a ball, a half capsule, a quarter cut from a drum. Today the kit cannot draw that surface.

Proposed: `from` and `to` options on `lathe`, in radians from `F.u` toward `F.v`, the same angles `arcOf` already takes. Defaults are `0` and a full turn, so nothing changes when they are not given.

```js
G.lathe(ballProfile, F, P, { from: Math.PI / 2, to: 2 * Math.PI, smooth: { slope } })
```

- Only that part of the revolution is drawn, and the flat faces where it was opened are drawn with it. A cut face is the profile itself laid in the plane at `from` and at `to`, so the profile is closed along the axis, as for `solidOf`. The section of the part comes for free: a hollow profile gives the wall as a ring.
- Each face is toned from its own normal, drawn only when it faces the viewer, and outlined. On an exact half turn the two faces are one plane, and the axis edge between them is not drawn.
- Shading is always the analytic smooth one (a partial turn has no facet fill), so `smooth: { slope }` works as it does today. `rims`, `bevel` and creases follow the part. `hole` with a partial turn throws, and so does `to <= from`.
- Marks on a cut face use `pointOf(F, s, r, from)` or `pointOf(F, s, r, to)`, so nothing new is needed for decals.

#### Prototype

The patch ([`u7.patch`](https://github.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/blob/issue-figures/u7/u7.patch)) is against `1482e84`. It changes `kit/lathe.mjs` (+105 −16: three small helpers, `smoothRows` takes the angle window, `lathe` builds its own outline for a partial turn), adds a paragraph each to `references/kit.md` and the changelog, and adds `scripts/lathe-partial-turn.test.mjs` (48 lines) with a ray-cast helper `scripts/lathe-truth.mjs` (168 lines). No comments, per CONTRIBUTING. [`u7-pages.patch`](https://github.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/blob/issue-figures/u7/u7-pages.patch) is the rebuilt arcade cabinet pages (see the first question).

![whole ball, quarter out, half capsule](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/issue-figures/u7/u7-whole-wedge-capsule-light.png)

Left to right: today's whole ball, the same profile with `from: π/2`, and a capsule with `from: π`. At 4× on the wedge's pole: ![wedge, 4x](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/issue-figures/u7/u7-wedge-4x-light.png)

A cylinder with a quarter out, and a half cylinder with `bevel: 2, rims: "first"` beside the whole one: ![cylinders](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/issue-figures/u7/u7-cylinder-bevel-light.png)

#### How I checked it

For each shape I ray-cast every other pixel of a 360 × 300 card through the same projection against the swept solid, took the tone from the smooth normal or the cut face's normal with `bandOf`, and compared it with the painted tone bands. Pixels whose 3 × 3 neighbours differ are skipped as edge pixels. Red is coverage, yellow is tone.

| shape | coverage mismatch | tone mismatch |
|---|---|---|
| ball, quarter out, camera azimuth 45° | 0 | 0 of 45 047 |
| same ball, azimuth 135° | 0 | 0 of 44 978 |
| same ball, azimuth 315° | 0 | **1 645 of 44 797 (3.67%)** |
| ball, half out | 0 | 0 of 45 320 |
| capsule, lower half | 0 | 0 of 45 349 |
| cylinder, three quarters | 0 | 0 of 45 534 |
| capsule shell (wall 3.5), lower half | 0 | **1 562 of 43 722 (3.57%)** |

![wedge check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/issue-figures/u7/u7-check-wedge.png)

- The 3.67% case is the far side of the notch. The face the viewer sees is partly hidden by the rest of the ball, and it is painted over it anyway: every mismatched pixel is in that face's tone. Faces and surface are bucketed by tone, not sorted by depth, so this is built in. A zoom looks into the notch, where it does not show, but the kit should say so. ![far side](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Don-Yin/anatomy/issue-figures/u7/u7-check-far-side.png)
- The shell's 3.57% is not explained. At a 3 px step, 234 of its 264 mismatched samples carry the lightest band, the cut face's tone, so it looks like the same family, but I have not separated "painted over the lining" from "my ray-cast's cut-versus-surface boundary is off near a thin wall". It could be the checker.
- `scripts/lines.mjs` reports `line ends: 0` on the sheet in both themes, and the console is clean.
- The committed tests: `lathe-partial-turn` (5 tests: three shapes at 0 coverage and under 0.1% tone, a full turn given as `from: 0, to: 2π` equal to no arguments, the two throws) passes. With `CHROME_PATH` set, the `audit-*`, `fidelity-cut`, `turn-convex-check`, `turn-rounded-polygon` and `turn-split-owner` files pass together with it (118 tests in all, the 5 new ones included). The three `audit-*` files that drive Chrome fail on a 30 s timeout without `CHROME_PATH` and pass (35 tests) with it. The five `react-*` files fail here with `Cannot find module 'typescript'` (no `npm install` in my copy); `react-solid-seamless` fails the same way on a clean `1482e84`, and I did not run the other four there.
- Every example and both themes, the turning dial with `--verify` and `stress.mjs --light`, rebuilt as in `ci.yml`. Only the arcade cabinet's two pages change (next section). Every other example is byte-identical.

### Kind of figure

SVG

### Why it is worth adding

I built four figures against an unmodified copy of the kit to see where it stops outside the machine examples: an attention grid, a neuron, a small neural net and a cell, mitochondrion, ATP synthase zoom (a #51-style recursive zoom, done by hand with `viewBox` tweens). The cell was the one that needed cutaways, and it hit these three, in the order they came up:

1. **No partial revolution.** Level 1 is an intact `sphereOf` shell with two cut faces painted over it. The sphere's silhouette stays whole, so the quarter a real wedge would remove is still drawn. It reads as a cutaway through the faces and the rim band, but it is not one.
2. **No cut face.** `disc` and `ringBand` are perpendicular to a lathe axis. A face in the cutting plane with a rim where the shell was cut went into a per-figure painter (`mesh.mjs`, 153 lines) as flat quads.
3. **No half-capsule trough.** `lathe` gives a full capsule and `stadium` with `prismOf` a capsule prism, and a capsule meridian over half the angle, with a lining and a rim at the cut, was another case in the same per-figure painter.

`from` and `to` cover the first fully for a lathe, and the second and third where the cut plane contains the axis, which is the common case. A quarter or half out of a ball, drum, bearing, valve or engine bell is the same call.

I am not claiming #51's computer, CPU, ALU figure needs this. Boxes are opened with slabs and prisms already, and I would expect your hand-built reference to get by on those. It is for the figures whose subject is round.

### What you tried instead

A per-figure painter for open surfaces, and a whole `sphereOf` with faces painted on it (described above). Neither goes through the kit's smooth shading, outline or `A.recorder`.

#### Questions

1. **`lathe.mjs` is inlined into the arcade cabinet's pages** (`latheSource` in its `build.mjs`), so any edit to the file changes those two pages by the same lines as the diff (+105 −16 each). The drawing data in them is unchanged (I compared the added and removed lines against `kit/lathe.mjs`, apart from the stripped `export`). CONTRIBUTING asks for byte-identical rebuilds, or the rebuilt pages in the same PR with a note. Do you want the rebuilt pages committed with the change, or should the arcade build inline only the helpers it uses first? The second would be a separate PR.
2. **Is `{ from, to }` on `lathe` the right shape?** The alternative is a separate `wedgeOf` or `cutawayOf`. I kept it on `lathe` so a bevel, rims and creases work on the part with no second code path to maintain. The cost is that `lathe` now has a second outline path for a partial turn.
3. **`sphereOf`.** I did not touch it. It builds a ball as four convex hulls of spherical caps, so it is cheap, and a wedge makes the caps non-convex, so `hullOf` cannot be used. The patch uses `lathe` for a ball: the same ball with a quarter out is 77.8 kB of path data at 24 knots (115 kB at 60), the whole ball through `lathe` is 38.7 kB, and `sphereOf` is 3.4 kB. Tone matches the ray cast at 0.00% at 16, 24, 36 and 60 knots, so 24 is enough. Is that cost acceptable for a handful of cutaways, or should `sphereOf` take `from` and `to` with its caps clipped against the wedge's projected outline? I think the second is the right end state, but it is a second, larger change and I did not prototype it.
4. **Why is the wedge twice the whole ball?** I tuned `smooth` rows (the ball's fill went from 37.3 kB to 33.6 kB) and did not isolate where the rest of the bytes go. If you can see a cheaper construction, say so.
5. **Depth.** Should the face be clipped against the rest of the body so the far-side view above is right, or is "look into the notch" enough for a documented limit? I put the limit in `references/kit.md` as written above.
6. **Cut planes that do not contain the axis** (a slice across a capsule, a disc on an arbitrary plane) are not covered. Should that be a separate helper, or left to `prismOf` and `extrude`?
7. **Audit.** `A.recorder` has shapes for turned bodies but I did not check how it should record a partial one, or whether `turn-build.mjs` live lathes should take `from` and `to`. Neither is touched.

I am not asking for a PR yet. If the shape is agreed I would send the patch (with the rebuilt arcade pages if you choose that), and look at `sphereOf` in a second PR.

### Before you submit

- [X] I searched the existing issues.
- [X] I read the Limits section of the README.

## What this changes

Adds two kit functions that draw on a vertical face what `onTop` and `planOutline` draw on a top face:

title: Add offsetPath: move a floor polyline sideways with mitred corners
body:
## What this changes

Adds `offsetPath(points, by, limit = 4)` to the kit: a floor polyline moved sideways by `by`, point for point.

- A positive `by` moves a path that runs along +x toward +y.
- Interior corners are mitred so both adjacent legs stay exactly `by` away; a mitre never reaches past `limit` × `by` from its corner (like SVG's `stroke-miterlimit`).
- Repeated points take the direction of their nearest real segment, so they move with their neighbours; a single point, or a path of one repeated point, stays put.

It is in `kit/iso-kit.ts` and `kit/iso-kit.mjs` (the transpiled output, unchanged elsewhere), listed in `references/kit.md` under "Solids" next to `insetPlan`, and covered by `scripts/offset-path.test.mjs`: straight paths both ways, square corners inside and outside, the exact `by` distance from both segments along a curve, the mitre limit on a hairpin, repeated points, and the TypeScript twin.

## Why

Two-edged things follow one centreline: both rails of a track, the edges of a belt, a lane, a road, a pair of parallel cables. The kit can `fillet`, `resample`, `cut` and walk a path, but not offset one, so a figure had to compute normals and corner joins itself. A railway-junction figure needed it for its bed, both rails and its sleepers.

title: Add sideDigit and sideDigits: numerals as strokes on vertical faces
body:
## What this changes

Adds three exports to the kit (`iso-kit.mjs` and `iso-kit.ts`):

- `sideDigit(digit, [u, z, w, h], at, "x" | "y", P)` draws one numeral as strokes in a box on a vertical face at `x = at` or `y = at`, reading the way the face is seen (on an x face, from high y to low y).
- `sideDigits(value, count, [u, z, w, h], gap, at, "x" | "y", P)` lays out a row of numerals odometer style (`12047` on four wheels shows `2047`).
- `DIGIT_STROKES` is the ten-glyph stroke font they use (`[u, z]` in a 1 × 2 box).

Callers draw the result with `lineSvg(d, { free: true })`. Docs: a row each in `references/kit.md` under "Lines on faces", and a line under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`. Tests: `scripts/side-digits.test.mjs` (5 tests, including that the TypeScript build gives the same output).

A second commit, **Turning dial: clear the four cable-end crowding pairs**, makes the full turn audit pass (main reports the same four `crowding` lines today):

- The green terminal moves from `x = 7.3` to `x = 0`, so the green cable ends just past its clamp. That clears both green pairs (finger 3 at 165°, the piston rod at 285°, where the old end read as the rod plugged into the terminal), and it still clears with the gap raised to 4 px.
- `["cable.red", "hand.f1.p1"]` and `["cable.blue", "hand.f3.p1"]` join the figure's `crowd` list. Those ends run parallel to the finger link their junction sits on, which `references/3d.md` says no offset clears; at 8× in both themes each reads as a cable plugged into the junction box with the link separate behind it, the same way the figure already lists the matching `p2` pairs.
- The audit and its thresholds are unchanged. Only the turning-dial pages change. The README's hero image (`.github/assets/turning-dial.webp`) still shows the old terminal position; nothing in the repo regenerates it, so I left it.

## Why

Counter wheels, meter windows and plate numbers on vertical faces had to be `faceTextSvg` text or hand-projected strokes. Text depends on the page's font and can't be audited as geometry; hand-projected strokes get copied between figures. As strokes, the numerals scale, print and update like any other line (`d` changes when the value does). I've been using this in a set of teaching figures with many live counters, and it's the one piece that seemed general enough for the kit.

title: print.mjs: reject option values it cannot use
body:
## What this changes

`--out` and `--format` now require their value, and an unknown `--format` is rejected right after the argument loop, before the spec module is imported.

## Why

Both flags read `argv[++index]` without checking that it exists. A flag left last became `undefined` and fell through the `??` chain, so the existing rejection in the same file — `unknown format "..."; use one of poster, drawing, detailed or all` — was bypassed by the one input that most looks like a mistake.

On `main`:

```
$ node scripts/print.mjs examples/raptor-engine/sheet.mjs --format bogus
Error: unknown format "bogus"; use one of poster, drawing, detailed or all   # exit 1

$ node scripts/print.mjs examples/raptor-engine/sheet.mjs --format
wrote raptor-engine-poster-a4.html (3202 KB) and raptor-engine-poster-a4.pdf (599 KB, 1 page)   # exit 0

$ node scripts/print.mjs examples/raptor-engine/sheet.mjs --out
wrote raptor-engine-poster-a4.html (3202 KB) and raptor-engine-poster-a4.pdf (599 KB, 1 page)   # exit 0
```

No shipped spec sets `format`, so a bare `--format` always prints the `poster` default and exits 0: the sheet is not the one asked for and nothing says so.

Separately, the unknown-format check ran after `await import(specFile)`, so a misspelled format on a figure whose light page is not built was reported as the missing page, or as a module error, rather than as the typo it was.

The later check is kept, because it still guards a `format` coming from the spec itself.

This is the same fix already recorded under Unreleased for `capture.mjs`, and matches `drive.mjs`, `lines.mjs`, `turn-check.mjs` and `turn-bench.mjs`.

## Tests

- `scripts/print-options.test.mjs`

It fails on `main` by name (`# pass 0 # fail 1`) and passes here (`# pass 1 # fail 0`). `node --test scripts/print-sheet.test.mjs scripts/print-options.test.mjs` is `# tests 12 # pass 12 # fail 0`.

Valid input still passes validation and is unaffected: `--format poster|drawing|detailed|all`, `--out <name>`, and no `--format` at all.

I did not run the full `scripts/*.test.mjs` suite (it needs Chrome and the temp react/typescript install). The change touches only `main()`'s argument parsing in `print.mjs`, which no other module imports.

## Checks

- [x] Every example rebuilds, and `git status --short` shows only the changes I meant. (No example or kit change; `git status --short` shows only `scripts/print.mjs`, `scripts/print-options.test.mjs` and `CHANGELOG.md`.)

- [ ] I built and looked at both themes. Not applicable: no visual change.
- [ ] Figures with pipes, cables or round parts. Not applicable: no figure change.
- [ ] `node scripts/lines.mjs`. Not applicable: no figure change.

title: Bug: reduced-motion changes do not stop in-flight animations in example patterns
Claude Code plugin: install with /plugin install anatomy@anatomy
body:
## What this changes

Adds `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, so Claude Code can install Anatomy as a plugin:

```text
/plugin marketplace add wheresryan22/anatomy
/plugin install anatomy@anatomy
```

The marketplace is named `anatomy` and lists one plugin, `anatomy`, whose `source` is `./`, the repository root. Claude Code loads a plugin with `SKILL.md` at its root and no `skills/` folder as a single skill, so no file moves and the skills CLI, git and ZIP installs keep working as before. The skill runs as `/anatomy:anatomy`, since plugin skills carry the plugin's name, and Claude still picks it up on its own from the description.

The README gets a row in the install table, an "As a Claude Code plugin" section and a line in the layout tree. `CHANGELOG.md` gets a line under Unreleased.

## Why

Adding the repo as a marketplace fails today. On `main`:

```text
$ claude plugin validate .
  ❯ directory: No manifest found in directory. Expected .claude-plugin/marketplace.json or .claude-plugin/plugin.json
✘ Validation failed
```

On this branch:

```text
$ claude plugin validate .
  ❯ plugins[0] plugin.json → version: No version specified. Consider adding a version following semver (e.g., "1.0.0")
✔ Validation passed with warnings
```

I left `version` out on purpose. With it set, Claude Code keeps every user on that string until someone bumps it, and the repo has no releases yet. Without it, the version is the commit SHA, so `claude plugin update anatomy@anatomy` picks up each commit on `main`. If you'd rather pin releases, add `"version"` to `plugin.json` and bump it per release.

Tested with Claude Code 2.1.288 on Windows, each time in a throwaway `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`:

- `claude plugin marketplace add <local clone>`, then `claude plugin install anatomy@anatomy`. `claude plugin details anatomy` lists `Skills (1) anatomy`, with no agents, hooks or MCP servers. `agents/openai.yaml` is not a `.md` file, so the plugin loader ignores it.
- `claude plugin marketplace add Azasratruth/anatomy@claude-code-plugin`, then `claude plugin install anatomy@anatomy`. `claude plugin list` shows `Version: a88a1f25c1ac`, `Status: ✔ enabled`, and the files land in `~/.claude/plugins/cache/anatomy/anatomy/a88a1f25c1ac/`.

One snag worth knowing about. Claude Code gives a marketplace clone 120 seconds, and my connection needed about 140 for the repo's 14 MB, so the first add failed with `Git clone timed out after 120s`. `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS=600000` got it through. Most connections won't notice, so I left it out of the README.

## Checks

- [x] Every example rebuilds, and `git status --short` shows only the changes I meant. I ran all 16 build commands from `ci.yml`. Three pages (`raptor-engine.html`, `raptor-engine-light.html`, `turning-stress-light.html`) came out with one changed float each, in the last digit, such as `0.4539904997395468` against `0.45399049973954675`. That looks like Node 24 on Windows rounding trig results differently from the macOS build CI compares against, and this PR touches no code. I didn't commit them; CI on macOS will show a clean tree.
- [x] No comments in code. The two new files are JSON.

title: Proposal: Parametric Surface Loft for Freeform Curved Geometry
body:
### What are you asking for?

A new example figure

### The idea

## Proposal: Parametric Surface Loft for Freeform Curved Geometry

### What are you asking for?

A new optional geometry primitive for generating smooth, freeform 3D surfaces from multiple cross-sectional profiles.

### Motivation

I've been experimenting with Anatomy to build interactive automotive visualizations.

The existing primitives, such as prisms, extrusions, lathes, and tubes, work well for mechanical components. However, I encountered limitations when trying to model smooth, non-axisymmetric surfaces such as vehicle hoods, fenders, and curved equipment enclosures.

A parametric surface loft could help address this limitation while remaining useful beyond automotive applications.

### Proposed Direction

I'm considering a general-purpose loft primitive that could:

- Accept multiple cross-sectional profiles.
- Interpolate between sections to generate smooth surfaces.
- Support configurable sampling resolution.
- Produce consistent surface normals and geometry suitable for rendering.
- Integrate with Anatomy's existing projection, shading, and geometry audit systems.
- Remain opt-in without changing existing examples or their output.

A possible conceptual API might look like:

```javascript
loftSurface({
  sections: [...],
  interpolation: "catmull-rom",
  resolution: [32, 16]
});
```

This is only an initial API concept, not an implementation proposal.

### Questions

Before working on an implementation, I'd appreciate your thoughts:

1. Would a general-purpose surface loft primitive fit Anatomy's intended scope?
2. Is there an existing primitive or recommended modeling approach that already addresses this use case?
3. Would you prefer this functionality as a standalone geometry module, an extension of the current primitives, or something else?
4. What would be the minimum acceptable scope for an initial PR?

I'd be happy to start with a small, independently verifiable example and follow the project's contribution and compatibility requirements.

Thanks for building and maintaining Anatomy!

### Kind of figure

Not about a figure

### Why it is worth adding

Anatomy's existing primitives work well for mechanical components with regular shapes, but modeling smooth, non-axisymmetric surfaces remains challenging.

While working on an interactive automotive visualization, I found that combining prisms, extrusions, and lathes often produces visibly faceted body panels rather than continuous curved surfaces.

A general-purpose parametric surface loft could fill this gap by interpolating between cross-sectional profiles. Beyond automotive applications, it could support equipment enclosures, aircraft shells, curved industrial panels, and other complex mechanical forms.

I believe this could expand Anatomy's modeling capabilities without changing its existing primitives or default behavior.

Before attempting an implementation, I'd like to ask whether this direction fits Anatomy's scope and what a suitable minimal implementation would look like.

### What you tried instead

I experimented with combining extruded profiles, convex prisms, and lathe-based geometry.

These approaches work for simplified mechanical shapes, but they are less suitable for surfaces whose cross-sectional shape changes continuously along multiple axes.

I also considered implementing a custom loft generator outside Anatomy, but wanted to check whether a reusable primitive would be valuable to the upstream project before proceeding.

title: fix(drive): stop Chrome and its helpers when the run ends or is terminated
body:
## What this changes

- `scripts/drive.mjs` stops Chrome and all of its helper processes together: Chrome is spawned in its own process group, one `SIGKILL` takes the whole group, and the driver waits until nothing of that group is left (bounded at 3 s) before it removes the profile folder. The same stop runs on a normal exit and when the driver itself is terminated (a test's 30 s timeout, Ctrl-C). After a termination it exits by the same signal it received, so callers see the exit status they always did. On Windows the behaviour is unchanged.
- `scripts/drive-signal.test.mjs` (new): starts a long `wait` action, sends `SIGTERM` once Chrome is running, then asserts that the driver died by `SIGTERM`, that no process using that profile remains, and that the profile folder is gone. Skipped on Windows.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: a line under Unreleased / Fixed.

## Why

A terminated driver run used to leave its headless Chrome running. Under `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` (the CI command, which runs test files in parallel), every browser test that hit its 30 s limit leaked a Chrome, each leak slowed the next test, and the run cascaded. On an 8-core laptop: 538 orphaned Chrome processes, a load average of 622, every browser test failing. The same suite serialised passed 289 of 290.

A normal exit also left near-empty profile folders behind (`Default/Reporting and NEL-journal`, `Default/Network Action Predictor-journal` and similar), written by Chrome processes that were still shutting down when the folder was removed.

Measured with this change on the same machine, full suite in parallel: 291 of 291 pass in 106 s, 0 Chrome processes and 0 profile folders left afterwards. The new test fails against the previous driver with `timed out waiting for Chrome to be gone`.

title: Harden the 3D runtime: multi-mount hooks, cycle breaking, group order
body:
## What

Three small fixes in the 3D runtime, applied identically to `kit/turn.mjs` and `kit/turn-fixed.mjs`, plus some dead-code cleanup.

1. **`window.__isoTurn` with several figures.** A second `TURN.mount` overwrote the first one's hook, so `drive`/`turn-check` could only reach the last figure. Every mount is now also listed in `window.__isoTurns`. `__isoTurn` still points at the latest mount, so existing scripts are unchanged. `destroy()` removes the mount from the list and falls back to the previous one instead of deleting the hook.
2. **`breakCycle` in `t3Order`.** It returned as soon as it found the first cycle, even when every edge of that cycle had already been checked. The caller then went straight to a forced pick, and other cycles that could be resolved were never examined. It now keeps scanning when the first cycle has no droppable edge.
3. **`t3Poses`.** A group whose `parent` index is not smaller than its own was silently treated as a root, giving a wrong pose. It now throws a clear error. The builder always creates parents first, so valid data is unaffected.
4. **Cleanup.** Removed unused `x0`/`x1`/`buf` in `t3EmitPrism` and a duplicated, mis-indented `lines.key.length = 0;` (prism and tube emitters).

## Testing

`node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` with the CI's test dependencies (react 19.3.0, react-dom 19.3.0, typescript 5.9.3, esbuild 0.28.2): **290/290 pass, both before and after** the change.

Note: no existing test forces a cycle that the old `breakCycle` could not resolve, so change 2 is not covered by a test. I can add a regression fixture if you point me at the preferred place.

## Not changed

`t3Gjk` approximates separation over sampled point clouds rather than the full solids, so its margin can be overestimated in edge cases. I left it alone, since changing it needs the orbit audits.

title: Fix Chrome profile cleanup and startup tests on Windows
body:
## Summary

Two small, related fixes so the headless-Chrome QA toolchain (`capture`, `drive`, `turn-check`) runs on Windows. Both patches are no-ops on POSIX behavior-wise, and the full startup test suite passes 3/3 on Windows 11 (10.0.26100), Node v24.19.0.

## Patch 1 — `scripts/chrome-port.mjs`: retry profile cleanup so a transient `EPERM` does not mask the real error

**First principles.** On Windows, a file cannot be deleted while any process holds an open handle to it. When Chrome fails to start and is killed with `SIGKILL`, kernel handle teardown is asynchronous: the dying child's handles to its `--user-data-dir` profile files can briefly outlive the kill. The current cleanup does a single synchronous unlink:

```js
rmSync(profile, { recursive: true, force: true });
```

A sharing violation (`EPERM`) on any profile file at that instant makes `rmSync` throw inside the `catch` block — the block whose entire job is to surface the *real* diagnostic (`Chrome exited before startup: ...`). The caller then sees a misleading `EPERM` instead of the actual cause, breaking the error contract that `chrome-startup.test.mjs` itself asserts on (`/Chrome exited before startup/`).

**Why the fix is principled rather than a workaround.** Node's `fs.rm` already implements exactly this semantics — `maxRetries`/`retryDelay` exist primarily because Windows sharing violations are a documented, transient filesystem behavior — so the patch simply opts into the platform-appropriate API:

```js
await rm(profile, { recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 12, retryDelay: 150 });
```

~1.8 s worst case, only spent when an `EPERM`-class error actually occurs; the POSIX happy path is unaffected. If cleanup still fails, both errors are wrapped in an `AggregateError` ("Chrome startup and profile cleanup both failed") so the original startup error is never lost — the diagnostic contract is preserved even in the worst case.

## Patch 2 — `scripts/chrome-startup.test.mjs`: make the fake-Chrome shim work on Windows

**First principles.** The test fabricates a `chrome` binary as a `#!/bin/sh` shell script with `chmod 0o755`. On Windows there is no `/bin/sh`, so spawning the shim fails *before any launcher logic runs* — the test never reaches the cleanup path it exists to verify. It's not that the test fails loudly; it fails in a way that tells you nothing about profile cleanup.

**Fix.** On `win32`, use `process.execPath` (Node itself) as the early-exit Chrome substitute: Node is always present, requires no new dependency, and invoking it with Chrome's arguments guarantees an immediate non-listening exit, exercising the same "Chrome exited before startup" cleanup path. Cleanup is then verified directly — snapshot the `iso-capture-` / `iso-drive-` / `turn-check-` prefixed temp profile directories before and after, and assert none leak. The POSIX path (shim script + receipt file) is kept byte-for-byte and remains the code path used on macOS/Linux.

## Testing

- Windows 11 (10.0.26100 x64), Node v24.19.0: `node --test scripts/chrome-startup.test.mjs` → 3/3 pass (~1.3 s).
- Patch applies cleanly on top of `1482e84` (current `main`).
- No behavior change on POSIX: same APIs are called, retries only activate on `EPERM`-class errors that essentially do not occur here, and the shim path is untouched.
